# 44. Consumer first-install and upgrade as a reversible transaction

**Packet:** DEEP-44 | **Lead:** BOT-01 | **Partners:** BOT-02 state/rights, BOT-03 local inference, BOT-09 toolchains, BOT-11 setup UI, BOT-12 independent device acceptance. **Source anchors inspected on main:** skeleton/app/first_install.py, skeleton/app/installer.py, skeleton/app/studio_readiness.py, skeleton/app/manifest.json, frontend/src/features/Setup/AppSetupWorkspace.tsx and the named offline install/recovery paths under skeleton/app. **Authority:** the already declared app/installation/identity/deployment owners; do not create a replacement installer.

The first-install acceptance bar is unusual for an AI game studio: the user must be able to install the product even when neither a large GGUF nor the native game compiler is available. First install succeeds at a progressively capable local operating state; higher features are admitted only after authenticated evidence, rather than guessed from installed files. This distinction is already visible in the inspected setup UI, which gives host commands for installation, configuring the installation owner, local model provisioning and app doctor. Treat that as an initial operator surface, not proof of a seamless consumer wizard. The highest-value extension is **a reversible, state-aware installer with a truthful first-playable journey**, not a second set of install scripts.

## 44.1 Host capability inventory before mutation

The install session starts with read-only host inspection and persists an operator-visible preflight report. The report includes supported OS/build/architecture, available logical CPU topology, RAM and pressure class, GPU vendor and safe measurable memory ceiling, system and temporary disk capacity, filesystem behavior, permission model, WSL and Docker availability where appropriate, virtualization prerequisites, network mode, power state, existing installs and known data roots. Hardware IDs, usernames, raw environment strings and private network addresses are not eligible for unredacted public issue reports. Distinguish **observed**, **declared**, **unknown**, **unsupported**, **operator-action-required** and **rejected**; a missing GPU does not mean the application cannot run in CPU-only mode, while a missing required durable data store can block protected write functionality.

Capacity computation must reserve headroom for OS, database, browser/editor, native toolchain, asset build cache, model runtime, KV and spill. Initial minimums are target-profile decisions backed by physical tests; do not derive universal gigabyte figures from LLM guesses. Choose bounded nonoverlapping paths for application, private credentials, model weights, durable user data, temporary build workers, cache and game-library exports. A detected older version must be handled as an upgrade candidate, not a new empty install. Reject filesystem locations that are unsafe under the platform's link/reparse-point and permission rules.

Preflight performs no privilege escalation or irreversible host changes. Installer-recommended driver/WSL/Docker repairs are separately authorized human tasks. If a host cannot satisfy a declared full-game target, offer a truthful restricted mode: source browsing/editor, deterministic reference game previews or CPU-only local inference where physically feasible. A feature manifest advertises actual active capabilities rather than a global "installed" boolean.

## 44.2 Install transaction journal and monotonic stage identity

Use the existing installation custody/reconciliation owner to represent a single install transaction with immutable transaction ID, target source version, source/package digest, host profile, old installed state, stage receipts, migration decision and rollback route. The explanatory stage sequence is:

**I-00 Discover:** read-only host and existing-data inventory. **I-01 Resolve:** architecture/source bundle and permitted offline dependencies. **I-02 Trust:** verify signature/digest/source policy and executable/active-content safety. **I-03 Capacity:** pre-reserve adequate bounded disk and allowed file roots. **I-04 Credentials:** create or reuse stable private application identities, never log them. **I-05 Stage:** place content in a new private immutable staging root, not the live installation. **I-06 Data backup:** consistent snapshots and schema/version/provenance records of all authoritative stores. **I-07 Migrate:** versioned, idempotent schema cutover under supported writer fences. **I-08 Services:** start database/engine/backend/frontend according to declared dependency order. **I-09 Verify:** authenticated protected health, route registry and operation readiness. **I-10 Studio:** prove an original real local game workflow for declared target; admit optional GGUF only after its independent guard. **I-11 Commit:** atomically switch the installed-version pointer, record evidence and preserve rollback assets within retention.

These labels are a specification for mapping existing real install logic, not permission to introduce conflicting state enums or user data stores. Stage receipts are versioned with precondition/source digests, allowed mutations, observed outputs, warnings and compensation. A completed stage must remain idempotent after power loss; rerun reads the receipt and validates its postcondition before deciding whether it needs to act again. A stage cannot generate new production secrets merely because a previous response was lost. If an old install is still actively serving, perform a supported quiesce/fence and verify writer state before migration, not a process sleep.

External installers and package managers may have unknown outcomes; reconcile their actual state before retries. On any failure, preserve prior user data and produce a plain-language exact recovery action, including paths to retained backups without disclosing secrets in a published report. A partial new runtime must not use the prior primary data store with incompatible schema. Checkpoint ordering must survive forced kill, disk-full and interrupted atomic rename.

## 44.3 Canonical database and local derived-index recovery

The machine/state_topology.json contract distinguishes primary Mongo authoritative domains, derived retrieval/vector stores, local process state and scoped SQLite receipts. Reuse each domain's declared consistency, migration, backup and retention semantics. Preserve independent identities of backend and engine Mongo logical databases where configured, while proving shared epoch and writer custody for protected cross-component operations. Do not create a "fresh clean database" behind the user's existing chat or project directory.

The known Chroma persistence risk—old /chroma/chroma versus pinned /data—requires nondestructive dual-source inspection before any mount change. Stop affected writers, identify container layer and volume contents, capture consistent snapshots with SQLite journal awareness, verify checksums and logical collection counts, stage migration to the intended current mount and independently query representative vectors/metadata after container recreation. Derived indexes may be rebuilt only from retained authoritative sources with current rights. Conflicting old/new Chroma contents trigger manual reconciliation; do not guess the newest source from filesystem modification time alone. If optional Chroma cannot be recovered safely, the app can expose an explicitly degraded lexical/reference mode where policy permits rather than destroy historical data to satisfy readiness.

Migration acceptance includes duplicate tenant IDs, interrupted batch, old process attempting to write, wrong replica-set topology, unknown schema version, driver downgrade, cache/state mismatch and missing backup. The fail-closed result protects authoritative state while keeping help/diagnostics reachable.

## 44.4 Local inference bootstrap as a separate verified capability

The inspected setup workspace already says downloading pinned weights alone does not make chat ready. Implement and prove the stronger chain: model download or offline import → byte size/digest verification → declared runtime/CPU/GPU compatibility → tokenizer and chat-template identity → architecture/policy bootstrap → reviewer and shared source epoch → canonical engine/provider admission → first authentic response → tool-authorized game edit. Each dependency has its own observed timestamp, scope, producer and recoverable failure reason. A valid offline source-only install must never silently activate an external provider or transmit project data to fetch "better" model performance.

A physical GGUF run needs actual model load, controlled memory profile, resource reservations, context and tokenizer attestation and bounded cancellation/recovery. Avoid inferring readiness from CLI --version or fixture success. If the model is too large for hardware, show smaller compatible profiles with their measured tradeoffs; never thrash virtual memory until the host becomes unusable. Persist model identity as source artifact with tested runtime compatibility so a later app upgrade does not replace known-good weights accidentally.

## 44.5 Router, service and UI readiness matrix

skeleton/app/first_install.py contains critical_backend_route_report, which checks observed live /api/health/registry critical_routes rather than trusting a 200 /health. That is a useful fail-closed seam. Extend product readiness consumers to distinguish registered routes, authenticated feature availability, correct principal scope, data stores, engine/provider, model and native toolchains. Public readiness returns no private details or authorization rights. Backend route presence is not proof that the route's implementation succeeds; exercise authenticated requests and selected denial probes separately.

The setup screen should be a progressive dashboard with host prerequisites, installed service state, missing actions, exact failing source of truth, repair command, safe recheck and last observed time. Keep setup UI usable even when engine, backend or model is unhealthy. No model or game build is required for browsing read-only setup. Buttons that claim "Repair" must actually route to an existing admitted repair operation or explicitly show a copyable host step; decorative controls or unbounded shell execution are not sufficient.

Required device matrix: first clean install; pre-existing data; upgrade with prior user project; missing Docker; unavailable model; wrong architecture; offline package; corrupted downloaded artifact; full disk; interrupted migration; invalid owner credentials; stale engine; bad Chroma mount; valid model but untrusted reviewer; UI reachable under backend outage; complete target game playable; source-preserving uninstall/repair. Record OS/versions and exact code/package digests. Release remains held wherever physical Windows/WSL2 or native GGUF proof is absent.

# 45. Creator cockpit: one coherent editing, simulation and AI-production workspace

**Packet:** DEEP-45 | **Lead:** BOT-11 | **Partners:** BOT-02 identity, BOT-04 orchestration, BOT-05 worlds, BOT-06 game runtime, BOT-08 media, BOT-09 exporter, BOT-12 accessibility/acceptance. **Inspected main source surfaces:** frontend/src/features/Jeeves/GamePlayViewport.tsx, GameFrontierAuthoringPanel.tsx, GameStudioReadinessPanel.tsx, WorkspaceController.ts, GameStudioAssistantPanel.tsx, CrawlerWorkspace.tsx, and the game/product clients. The current frontend has many specialist panels; the completion task is to assemble them into a comprehensible creator's experience without suppressing advanced functions or inventing frontend authority.

## 45.1 Intent-preserving creator workflow

A creator opens a project and sees six persistent conceptual domains: **Design**, **World**, **Play**, **Assets**, **Build**, and **Proof**. These are navigational views over existing records, not six new data stores. The global header shows project name and revision, authenticated owner, dirty/committed state, active finite AI jobs, current target, capability availability, save/recovery status and conflicting proposals. A context side pane shows selected scene/entity/asset, provenance, dependencies, validation errors, editable properties and expected downstream impact. A bottom activity surface provides real operation events, logs and evidence—not freeform model "progress thoughts" disconnected from durable state.

For novices, offer an assisted happy path: describe game → review options → create editable first scene → play with real controls → inspect issues → modify → rebuild → export. For experts, preserve granular typed editors, constraints, scene hierarchy, world event timeline, raw source view, input map, shader/asset inspector, performance traces, build graph and cause/effect debugging. Novice mode may hide complexity but must never produce a separate lower-integrity project variant. Project switching cancels or fences stale views; it does not silently cancel physical work or publish another project's mutation.

## 45.2 One authoritative project/session projection

Frontend local state is a UI projection: selection, open tabs, scroll, draft input, unsaved patch and ephemeral render cache. Canonical project revision, tool action results, play state, chat transcript and work progress come from the declared backend/engine authority. The inspected WorkspaceController already has a single-writer observable store, canonical-thread references, transport progress, retry fencing and injectable transport/storage. Extend these good patterns, rather than building a disconnected editor chat that assumes replies are durable.

Every async request carries actor/session epoch, project ID, expected project revision and finite cancellation token. An auth change, project switch, source revision mismatch or user cancellation must fence stale results before React state mutation. Do not let an earlier network response replace a newer project view or resurrect private data from a previous account. On reconnect, request authoritative state and event cursor, merge only accepted local drafts and preserve explicit conflicts. A frontend toast saying "saved" should appear only after the actual owner acknowledged a committed revision.

Dirty work recovery needs an authenticated local draft queue encrypted or otherwise protected according to platform/data class, bounded retention and explicit logout behavior. A browser's localStorage is not an authoritative source; offline edits are local proposals until replayed through CAS and rights checks. If a device restarts mid-edit, show "unsubmitted draft" versus "committed revision" unambiguously. Multiple open tabs/devices must detect conflicting edits and let the user inspect semantic diffs before merge.

## 45.3 Semantic game editors instead of static forms

The world editor should support scene-tree navigation, hierarchy and layers, brushes, entity placement, terrain/topology, collision affordances, tile/sprite and mesh binding, prefab instances, triggers, quests, dialogue, weather and cinematic timeline, while preserving real canonical operation IDs. The inspected GameFrontierAuthoringPanel exposes a large catalogue of terrain/structure/encounter operations over a live authenticated project. A long toolbar list is not sufficient usability: operations need searchable taxonomy, tooltips, typed parameters, preview, constraints, undo and actual compilation. Distinguish geometry operations that affect engine scenes from descriptive projections that propose content.

For each edit show exact impacted nodes and dependent outputs. Editing a door collision shape can affect navigation, quest feasibility, physics, animation and player playtest. The build graph should preview affected cost and tests before commit. An agent proposing 100 operations presents a summarized grouped diff and the ability to inspect any individual mutation. A "bulk apply" must still be an authorized finite transaction with all mandatory preconditions; failed partial application returns a stable rollback/recovery record.

Timeline UX needs multiple synchronized views: world story chronology, playable simulation ticks, animation clips, audio cues and cinematic track; never conflate logical game tick with real audio sample time or browser wall clock. Each view shows source origin and engine mapping where available. Users can scrub previews without mutating authoritative game state; a "commit at tick" action is a separate explicit test or game operation.

## 45.4 Live play viewport fidelity and input ownership

GamePlayViewport.tsx already maps keyboard and Gamepad controls to authenticated runtime play requests and handles recordings. That provides a concrete path toward a full studio cockpit. The next step is proving the viewport is synchronized with actual packaged engine state and the input mapping used by release. An authenticated server-side play session and a native Godot executable are not necessarily equivalent; expose their proof levels and map authoritative state/logic differences instead of declaring them identical.

Input capture must handle focus, key-repeat, browser shortcuts, gamepad connect/disconnect, axis deadzones, touch control accessibility, pause/background events and fast release of held buttons. If the viewport loses focus, bounded release input must reach the authoritative session without spuriously continuing player movement; if network drops, clearly suspend or use a separately admitted offline local simulation mode. Never mutate canonical inventory or quest state directly from DOM key handlers. Session identity and recording permission must be scoped to the active project and actor.

Replay UX shows exact source/game package, engine/version, seed, initial save, input trace, known nondeterministic tolerances, observed frames/audio and completion status. User can compare two play runs, jump to divergent ticks, inspect quest/world diffs, and create a bug repro linked to source. A local animated approximation may help editor responsiveness but must be labeled "preview" when it does not use the final runtime path.

## 45.5 AI-assisted editing with inspectable autonomy

Jeeves appears alongside the selected project object and may draft a proposal, produce alternative designs, explain a dependency, request a scoped tool operation or interpret a failed playtest. Do not implement "AI magic" as client-side direct provider calls. Every tool-bearing operation routes through current canonical ToolManifest/ToolExecutionRequest/Receipt and project revision CAS. The operator sees what data will be read, the exact files or entities to change, resource budget, deadline, expected side effects, reversibility and postconditions. A suggested action cannot become an approved action because a model writes "approved" in its reply.

Support steerable execution: pause after design; ask for a visual proof; redirect focus to collision; replace a source asset; request smaller target; inspect a candidate before committing. Steering must create an authorized new operation/revision decision. A bot running on an obsolete source revision must be forced to re-evaluate before writing. The UI shows **planned**, **running**, **blocked**, **awaiting approval**, **verifying**, **committed**, **rejected** and **reconciling unknown outcome** using canonical status mappings.

Human agency acceptance: an artist can override colors, textures, poses and dialogue without regeneration wiping changes; a designer can keep a disliked but intentional mechanic; and a user can disable AI while continuing to edit and play already built games. Any automatic regeneration must declare how it treats manual edits and use stable semantic IDs to avoid overwriting them.

## 45.6 Accessibility, internationalization and large projects

Keyboard-only navigation, screen reader labels, contrast, text scaling, reduced-motion animations, controller navigable command palette, remappable keys and game-specific accessible cues must work from setup to export. An accessibility editor should check not just panel WCAG-like properties but the game being authored: color-only puzzles, tiny timed inputs, flashing effects, captions and alternate interaction routes. Localization is versioned project content with string IDs, length/layout budgets, plural rules, subtitles and right-to-left handling where supported. The app should not invent unsupported language support; a translated label with broken gameplay text is not a complete locale.

Large project performance needs virtualized scene trees, lazy inspector panels, indexed search, bounded media thumbnails, progressive loading, selective build statuses and memory-aware 3D previews. Do not push thousands of full prefab documents into one React state object or render all scenes to show an outline. Client cache must honor tenant/revision invalidation and memory pressure, and it should never retain deleted private artifacts across logout.

## 45.7 Creator cockpit acceptance matrix

Run actual authenticated user journeys in web and supported native interface: create project; author world; create/delete character; connect a quest; edit collider; preview movement; save/restart; agent proposes edit; reject one and approve another; play; encounter a bug; inspect real trace; fix; export; reopen old project; switch account while a request is in flight; lose network; reconnect with local draft; use keyboard-only navigation and a gamepad. Test on a realistic large synthetic project and on an actual small exported game. Each button/field must either execute a bound operation or clearly be a read-only/proposed feature. The independent tester may record intermediate screenshots, but they do not replace observed authoritative actions.

# 46. Product runtime seam: source-level forge operations versus engine-executed gameplay

**Packet:** DEEP-46 | **Lead:** BOT-06 | **Partners:** BOT-05 world/IR, BOT-07 generators, BOT-08 media, BOT-09 export, BOT-12 verification. **Source anchors:** skeleton/forge/game_frontier_studio.py describes declarative portable editing that returns proposals for canonical Godot/engine confirmation; GameFrontierAuthoringPanel and gamePlayClient consume authored and play state; multiple Godot adapters exist. The hard work is proving the actual lowering and runtime equivalence, not inventing more symbolic operations.

## 46.1 One action, multiple representations, one semantics

An action such as "player picks up key and unlocks door" may appear in a semantic world graph, a forge edit, an exported GDScript event, an engine signal, a UI log, and a saved-game event. These representations must agree on stable action identity, preconditions, side effects, idempotency and replay behavior. Define an **ActionSemanticsWitness** as a test receipt (not a new independent source of truth) mapping semantic rule ID → compiled source/scene nodes → real input event → observed engine state change → persisted world event → visual/audio output. Any missing link is a qualification gap.

Create an engine mapping registry under the established exporter/target owner. Each supported operation declares what it lowers to, target feature requirements, unsupported cases, parameter bounds, emitted scripts/resources, runtime state readback and verification driver. Never generate an operation silently as a no-op; if a target cannot express a semantic rule, block that export or produce a user-approved explicit approximation with changed design spec and fresh tests.

## 46.2 Typed event-compiler protocol

For each authored event, validate trigger, condition, action, target and value against the real schema (game_frontier_studio.py already defines bounded StudioEvent types and finite trigger/action sets). Compile only validated safe symbols, not free-form model text that becomes GDScript or arbitrary shell command. Bind scene-node identities and user-authored rights. Escape strings and identifiers for the target language, enforce limits on recursion/iterations and reject unsupported foreign code execution. Target code runs with game's own permissions, not the app's service secrets.

Event example: a collision trigger checks an inventory key; it consumes or retains the key according to authored semantics, opens a door once, emits a quest flag and audible cue, and produces a SaveEvent. On repeated collision or replay after restart, no duplicate item grant occurs. The same semantic rule evaluated by the deterministic reference model and Godot driver must produce equivalent state under the declared event ordering. Engine frames are independently captured so "open door" visibly changed geometry/collision.

## 46.3 Player controller input-to-physics translation

Normalize gamepad/keyboard/touch input to a stable input action schema with device origin, timestamp/tick, action phase, analog amplitude and remapping profile. Distinguish "pressed", "held", "released" and "repeated"; one frame of an action must not be mistaken for indefinite hold. Godot input processing and physics fixed ticks must define sampling, interpolation and authoritative event commit boundaries. For networked or remote previews, specify buffering, sequence and latency bounds without assuming deterministic remote frame timing.

Collision/locomotion tests exercise jump buffer, slope, moving platform, portal crossing, constrained trigger volumes and player-camera occlusion for relevant genre. A reference algorithm may differ from actual Godot physics; define allowed tolerances and ensure tests detect material gameplay differences. Falling through a bridge, continuing motion after control release, wrong collision masks and input duplication must fail independent play checks.

## 46.4 Simulation versus exported runtime parity suite

Build an independent set of golden action traces for supported systems: quest flag, item grant/consume, door unlock, NPC notice/rumor, damage, save/reload, dialogue choice, timed trigger, puzzle mechanism and movement. Each trace specifies initial semantic state, source/target versions, step sequence, expected high-level invariants and observed native state. Run the same trace through the reference simulator and an exported Godot session. Compare state at explicit synchronization points, not merely final text. Differences may reveal an exporter bug, reference bug, unmodeled engine behavior or an unjustified assumption; record diagnosis and smallest patch owner.

Require three divergence tests that are capable of failing the suite: alter one GDScript transition, remove one collision signal and change an inventory amount in the native side. The harness should reject all three. A suite that still passes after severing the engine adapter is not integration proof. Capture source SHA, toolchain executable hash, exported game digest, test driver and observed state/frame artifacts to prevent stale green receipts.

## 46.5 Cross-target semantics and unsupported capabilities

Define a target capability subset of the common game IR. An HTML maze, a 2D Godot RPG and a 3D native racing game may share goal/state concepts but not the same input/physics/renderer semantics. Compile-to-web or console adapters must explicitly declare which events, media, save methods, controllers and safety restrictions they support. Unsupported events are hard errors or reviewed degradations, never empty stubs disguised as success. Stable core mechanics are more important than nominally supporting every engine under one generic interface.

When comparing engines, classify **bitwise deterministic**, **logical equivalent**, **perceptually equivalent** and **unsupported** behavior, with appropriate tolerance and proof. Physics may be logically equivalent despite frame timing differences; a color-only UI that hides a required goal is not perceptually equivalent for accessibility. The common semantics contract must preserve enough information to test these distinctions.

# 47. Simulation architecture for deep RPG, sandbox and multi-world games

**Packet:** DEEP-47 | **Lead:** BOT-05 | **Partners:** BOT-06 deterministic action engine, BOT-07 procedural generation, BOT-08 audiovisual world, BOT-09 save/export, BOT-12 simulation proof. **Status:** PROPOSED deeper integration over existing quest, scene, world-event and game-mechanics modules. Do not treat these features as absent merely because their target proof is unverified.

## 47.1 Multi-scale world time and causality

Separate gameplay fixed tick, world-calendar step, background simulation epoch, cinematic presentation time and real-world monotonic task clock. Each subsystem documents conversion and pause rules. Sleeping at an inn may advance world calendar and jobs but not duplicate combat input; a cutscene may pause player control but not the whole simulation if the design requests real-time background activity. Clock changes must be committed as typed world events and followed by deterministic dependent updates.

Simulation partitions: active high-fidelity region (per-frame entities and physics), adjacent regions (lower-frequency path/economy AI), distant regions (aggregate deterministic transitions), dormant authored states (reconstructed by seed and event summaries). Promotion between fidelity tiers has a reconciliation rule: commitments from coarse simulation become concrete entities/events with stable IDs and conserved resources. A travelling trader must not appear in two regions because both generated it during independent activation. Streaming regions must preserve ordered causal transactions and authority fences.

## 47.2 Regional society, economy and faction dynamics

Model economic resources as typed stock-flow systems with production, consumption, transfer, prices, scarcity and conservation invariants. Player purchases, quest rewards, crafting and NPC trades interact with one canonical currency/item ledger for the game session. A market stall selling a rare item must actually reduce stock; a crafted item must consume declared components; a faction embargo must alter supply routes and gameplay. Inflation and dynamic pricing are optional authored features, not excuses for chaotic untestable behavior.

Faction state includes reputation by actor/group, witnessed events, treaties, trade access, hostility, territory, goals and conflict rules. NPC rumors inherit observation and reliability. Simulate city logistics and ownership with deterministic event outcomes where practical. Prevent negative inventory, item duplication, unbounded prices, infinite trade arbitrage and social effects from hidden omniscience. Procedural regions must satisfy minimum resources for mandatory quests, or provide a verified migration/fallback path.

## 47.3 Quest planner and encounter director as bounded search

World and mission generation use hierarchical structures: chapters → acts → scenes → quests → encounters → atomic actions. For each goal, derive a causal plan with preconditions, resource budgets, alternative routes, fail/softlock recovery and witnessed completion. Use typed predicate graphs and bounded search (graph algorithms, constraint solvers or simulation) for feasibility; no unbounded recursive model call loop. High-level authored creativity remains human-editable and source-provenant. An NPC plan cannot change a quest condition simply because the player took an unexpected route.

An encounter director adapts enemy mix, recovery windows and environmental pressure based on observable play state with explicit fairness ceilings. It may adjust pacing but must not rewrite signed world history, player inventory or irreversible choices. Record adaptation inputs and policy version for replay and quality evaluation. Prevent feedback loops where higher difficulty causes lower player health, causing an even harder encounter. Use bounded hysteresis and opt-out policies, especially for accessibility.

## 47.4 World navigation, routes and spatial consistency

Stable location IDs, canonical coordinate frames, local origins and transform composition govern portals, floating islands, dungeons, vehicles and multiverse transitions. A route can exist semantically while being physically blocked by collision/terrain; both graph and engine traversal must be checked. Crossing a portal should preserve player identity, inventory, time and required quest state while changing allowed world context. Failed loads retain the original safe location and one authoritative transfer outcome.

Pathfinding must reflect terrain slope, climb/jump ability, doors, current faction access, environmental hazards, moving obstacles and dynamic costs. Use hierarchical nav meshes/graphs to bound enormous maps and replan only affected regions when terrain changes. For a 3D world, verticality and collision shape matter; two polygons connected in a map do not guarantee the player can traverse the actual scene. Independent agent input traces verify at least one feasible route for mandatory scenes.

## 47.5 Save, replay and massive variation correctness

Use stable seeds for authored environmental variation with explicit RNG stream version, but treat meaningful persistent world mutations as durable events. A world can have a huge procedural possibility space without storing every realized state. Content-addressed generated regions and aggregate snapshots reduce storage while preserving observed consequences. A save must retain required event ancestry and rights-aware media references; garbage collection cannot remove a dependency still needed by a live save or approved export.

Acceptance campaigns: 10,000 or more simulated offscreen steps within a declared bounded test envelope; deterministic replay under fixed seed/implementation; no duplicate unique IDs across streamed regions; no negative conserved resources; two causally distinct endings; player transfer across regions while save/reload occurs; NPC knowledge restricted to observations; economy updates during world-clock jumps; late quest edit invalidates dependent missions but not all unrelated art. These are proposed tests, not results. Report memory, CPU, storage and actual user-visible quality, not just the number of procedural configurations.

# 48. Verification laboratory and anti-gaming evidence

**Work packet:** DEEP-48 | **Lead:** BOT-12 | **Partners:** BOT-02, BOT-05, BOT-06, BOT-07, BOT-08, BOT-09. **Source directly inspected:** skeleton/forge/playtest.py runs a bounded Godot headless import and main-scene startup, scanning parse and runtime logs; its own source documents binary provenance and the distinction between a verified artifact-plane executable and a caller/PATH-provided unverified binary. This is genuine dynamic smoke evidence, not a complete input-driven game proof.

## 48.1 Claim-calibrated verification levels

For each proposed product capability, define the minimum experiment whose failure would contradict the claim. A game source file can be proven with hashes, but game playability requires an actual engine launch and controller actions that produce observed objective changes. A game that boots for 300 frames without parse errors is not necessarily traversable or winnable; a fixture reporting "win" is not equivalent to the exported game running on a clean target. An exported source project is not the same as a signed native executable. A working test on Windows CI is not by itself a supported consumer-device install certification. Keep these differences visible in the user cockpit and machine evidence.

Proof layers: **structural source**, **type/static**, **pure deterministic unit**, **multi-owner integration**, **real service**, **real engine and interactive input**, **exported clean-host**, **physical device**, **independently authorized release**. Map each positive claim to one or more layers, and retain explicit failure/pending/skipped/unobserved states for mandatory checks. All proof references bind source SHA, game project revision, canonical policy, toolchain executable digest, input workload, test runner, scorer and actual output artifact. Evidence from an ancestor commit expires when a relevant dependency changes. A verifier cannot upgrade source-only success merely by reading the builder's prose.

## 48.2 Model-based testing of project and game state

Generate command sequences against the **real** bounded application: create project; edit tile, actor, world rule and quest; inspect preview; commit revision; request AI work; start play; move/jump/interact; collect reward; save; restart; replay; delete or restore an asset; export. Include rejected commands: unknown project, wrong actor, stale revision, changed idempotency input, impossible terrain, forbidden source, oversized payload and unaudited script. After each accepted action assert invariants: revision monotonicity, typed source/rights references, valid world graph, finite resource usage, no duplicate rewards, no cross-tenant leakage, no unpublished artifact in public view and no active unauthorized worker.

Property-based tests should generate both small syntactically valid gameplay worlds and adversarial invalid ones. Constrain valid generations so failures are informative rather than universally rejected. Shrink complex counterexample sequences down to reproducible minimal steps with exact source/seed/environment. Preserve a regression test for every genuine defect found. A test that is guaranteed to pass because it only checks the generator's own claimed success string is invalid.

## 48.3 Differential proof between reference and Godot

For each supported action family, create a *logical projection* of the pure reference state and the native engine state. Replay the same initial game specification, fixed random seeds and action trace. Compare inventory ownership, quest flags, door/portal access, enemy damage, player checkpoint, dialogue choice, world-time changes and save data at defined synchronization points. Floating-point physics may need justified tolerances and platform-specific frames, but integer currency and idempotent quest grants should not. Record timing semantics so a harmless frame drift does not become a false source defect.

Metamorphic assertions expose hidden coupling: replacing a decorative particle asset must not change loot; changing a UI font must not change NPC factions; an identical idempotency request must not mint a second item; changing a collision shape must invalidate movement and navigation playtests; removing a source license must invalidate dependent exports even if rendered bytes are unchanged. Deliberately break one native signal, one gameplay reward and one save migration to prove the integration oracle detects actual engine divergence.

## 48.4 Forced crashes and unknown outcomes

Interrupt operations at every irreversible boundary: after resource reservation; after the project write but before its receipt; after outbound tool action but before durable reconciliation; halfway through asset import; before stream terminal; during Chroma volume migration; during save publication; during export signing; after provider payment callback but before entitlement; and after physical cancellation request but before worker exit. Restart the real owning service. Verify exactly one committed result or a truthful quarantined unknown outcome; no lost canonical user data, duplicate economy effect, stale source overwrite, leaked worker capacity or false "success" stream event.

The test harness must exercise process kill/restart or equivalent real failure, not only throw an exception inside a mocked function. Rebuild derived caches from authoritative state where policy permits. Inspect physical worker state before returning GPU/CPU memory reservations. Where an external side effect is uncertain, query or reconcile rather than blindly retry with a new identity.

## 48.5 Independent game quality and fairness

Create distinct tester profiles—novice, expert, explorer, accessibility, speedrun and adversarial—and let them interact through the actual game input path. An AI builder cannot author its own final scorer after seeing outputs. Hold out seeds and source briefs from optimization. Metrics include completion, softlocks, discoverability, fairness, input latency, player choice, visual style consistency, audible cues, accessibility, asset rights and user satisfaction. Subjective fun and art merit need blinded human review with disagreement and sample-size reporting; do not invent exact quality scores or promise universal delight.

A performance win that makes the game unwinnable, breaks captions or degrades privacy fails the noncompensable gates. The release evidence owner collects all required checks on the exact head; Secret Scanning success cannot neutralize Malware Gate failure, and source compile cannot neutralize actual target failure.

# 49. Safety architecture for an AI game-production toolchain

**Work packet:** DEEP-49 | **Lead:** BOT-02 | **Partner owners:** BOT-03 model, BOT-04 tools, BOT-08 media, BOT-09 packages, BOT-10 Dragon, BOT-12 independent security. Reuse the current declared identity, governance, tool, artifact and release planes. Do not create shadow permission or provider authority.

## 49.1 Security boundaries by input type

Inputs to the game studio may be hostile even when they look like creative assets: prompts, web pages, imported project files, binary meshes, compressed textures, shader code, animation metadata, game saves, generated scripts, tool manifests, model weights, package install metadata and repository PR content. Every payload is tagged by trust origin, tenant, admitted purpose, type, size and allowed operations. Data in a user's scene is not automatically privileged executable code. A crawler's instructions never become an agent's system prompt. A game export cannot inherit server secrets merely because both run on the same laptop.

Every protected mutation requires authenticated principal, scoped tenant/project, explicit delegated capability, approved tool manifest and bounded execution. The deterministic owner—not an LLM-generated answer—validates grants, arguments digest, expiry, source version, resource budget and postconditions. A replayed approval is not valid for a changed request body. Unknown tool definitions and unoffered functions are rejected before side effects.

## 49.2 Safe file trees and hostile media

Native extraction/build operations need descriptor-anchored file handling and defenses against symlinks, parent-directory replacement, Windows reparse points, archive traversal, Unicode/case collisions, special files, decompression bombs and excessive tree depth. A Path.resolve() followed by an unguarded read may be vulnerable to races; test actual implementation against concurrent swaps rather than treating a string-prefix comparison as sufficient. Limit files, expanded bytes, parser memory, recursion, CPU time, disk IO, process count and open file descriptors. Reject platforms on which required confinement guarantees cannot be met.

Execute compiler/import/asset processors under restricted identities with bounded source and output roots and no production credentials. Disallow arbitrary network access by default. Never let a model-proposed shell string directly become a privileged system command. Separate user-approved advanced plugin execution from normal game content parsing. A source package that contains executable payloads needs explicit policy and malware analysis before publishing it. Store scan status as completed-clean, finding, pending or unavailable, never as a binary unqualified green.

## 49.3 Immutable provenance and original-work rights

Every generated or imported asset needs canonical ArtifactRecord lineage: source bytes and digest, creator/license, transformation chain, model identity where relevant, permitted use, attribution, expiry/revocation, tenant, data class and dependent outputs. A publicly accessible image is not inherently reusable commercially. An AI-generated likeness or voice requires appropriate original source rights and consent. Rights to prototype are not automatically rights to monetize or redistribute. A revoked source propagates to derived media and public export eligibility, including cached packages, without erasing unrelated original artwork.

Game models, toolchains and dependencies need immutable byte identity and origin. A filename or version string is insufficient. Build evidence includes relevant dependency inventories, executable/scanner identity, scan findings, target architecture and rollback references. Treat model files as untrusted complex data parsed by native libraries even when inference itself is offline. Do not embed private chats, restricted research or secrets in fine-tuning datasets without explicit allowed processing and withdrawal support.

## 49.4 Cross-domain injection campaign

Attack via a page telling Dragon to access a private network; a repository README instructing Jeeves to expose credentials; a generated shader requiring shell execution; a ZIP with traversal; a fake source license; a project note spoofing a system role; an LLM tool proposal widening the grant; a modified artifact digest; and a tenant switch racing an in-flight editor request. Each negative test asserts no unauthorized filesystem/network/DB mutation and a durable denial or quarantine receipt. Quality is irrelevant if an accepted path bypasses authority. Unknown scanner results keep publication held.

# 50. Real-time QoS, device economics and adaptive physical scheduling

**Work packet:** DEEP-50 | **Lead:** BOT-03 and BOT-06 | **Partners:** BOT-07, BOT-08, BOT-09, BOT-11, BOT-12. Two workloads share a laptop: foreground playable real-time game state and background AI generation/build. They need separate latency objectives, but a single canonical capacity/admission authority. Never use logical virtual-worker counts as physical device evidence.

## 50.1 Latency and capacity budget vectors

Profile CPU execution, GPU memory and queue, physical RAM, page/swap pressure, disk throughput/latency, model KV, active model weights, decoder/renderer memory, build process slots and thermal/power state where observable. Reservation and actual utilization are distinct. A resource vector belongs to tenant, operation, workload class, exact model/game target, deadline and finite release receipt. When a cancellation is requested, keep the capacity reserved until the physical worker actually stops or is fenced by verified isolation. Unknown worker state blocks unsafe overcommit.

Measure end-to-end latency: input acquisition, server transport if used, game tick, world-rule evaluation, render submission, GPU output and user-visible display; separately track model queue wait, time to first usable design, time to actual game preview and time to complete accepted export. Report p50, p95 and p99 with workload/sample size and source/toolchain identity. A mean FPS or peak tokens/s without tail behavior is not sufficient.

## 50.2 Scheduler priorities and safety hysteresis

Protected interactive game frames and current user input must not be starved by unattended 3D asset synthesis. Interactive editing/chat jobs should be bounded and fairly admitted. Batch media, indexing, learning and compilation may be throttled, queued or safely checkpointed under pressure. Avoid abrupt oscillating admission by using measured multi-signal pressure states and hysteresis. Evict rebuildable caches before durable state; never free GPU reservations optimistically while the native process remains alive. Preserve last-good project commits when a low-memory situation forces cancellation.

The combined stress test runs real gameplay while Jeeves generates an asset and Dragon performs a genuinely approved bounded capture. Inject GPU pressure, large scene streaming, disk full, system suspend, backend restart and model timeout. Success requires the game remains within its declared target limits and background jobs either finish under bounded resources or pause safely with truthful status. Unmeasured host pressure remains unknown; do not fabricate sensor values.

## 50.3 Large-world and media streaming

Stream by spatial interest, gameplay relevance, rights validity and current performance budget. Use content-addressed region cells, stable world identities, actor-event continuity, prioritized asset IO and bounded GPU upload. Apply level-of-detail to geometry, textures, animation and distant NPC simulation while preserving collision, quest information and visual cues. Shader precompilation, import cache and image atlas optimization are candidates; measure frame-time outliers and memory against a retained reference version.

A streaming region cannot reappear with a different merchant inventory because the renderer unloaded it. Cosmetic RNG must be decoupled from quest and loot RNG. Dynamic prefetch must not follow untrusted network instructions. When assets are absent, show correct loading/fallback states without pretending a mandatory quest trigger exists. A game that briefly boots but stutters catastrophically during play is not a high-quality released target.

## 50.4 Power and thermal behavior

Handle AC/battery mode where observable, host sleep/resume, thermal throttling, WSL/container capacity differences and background workload suspension. Do not alter host safety controls or privileged system settings automatically. Profile sustained mixed-load performance rather than cold-start peaks only. If hardware telemetry is missing, prefer conservative limits and label measurement incomplete. Hardware support claims need representative physical device acceptance, not just resource calculations in source.

# 51. Exact product maturity and completion graph

**Work packet:** DEEP-51 | **Coordinator:** Grokbot | **Independent verdict:** BOT-12. The 421 existing AI masterplan volumes, 301 prior work orders, 42 already-done P0 tasks and hundreds of source modules are real scope and historical work. None alone prove the final product. Measure completion by demonstrated user journeys J-01..J-18 and supported target profiles.

## 51.1 Fixed evidence matrix

Each journey receives separate fields: source implemented, cross-plane integrated, actual live behavior observed, independently executed on target, release authorized. Keep qualitative holds for security, rights, state durability, install and exact-head CI. A weighted summary may be shown only if denominator, weights, workload and date/head are fixed and public to operators. A source volume cannot score full completion because it contains hundreds of thousands of lines. A model cannot self-award 95% completion. The weakest noncompensable required gate remains visible regardless of aggregate score.

## 51.2 Dependency-first implementation order

**Wave A:** canonical owner/current-head reconciliation, shared AI tree, backend route health, state writer topology. **Wave B:** reversible setup/install with stable secrets, safe Mongo/Chroma and offline source custody. **Wave C:** actual guarded GGUF through canonical provider with tokenizer/epoch/reviewer and authenticated tool work. **Wave D:** one original playable game from user brief, semantic world graph, real engine input, media, save/undo and editor. **Wave E:** clean native export, actual end conditions and source rights. **Wave F:** crash/retry, adversarial injection, device benchmarking, release gate and human approval. **Wave G:** broader genres, longform worlds, high-fidelity rendering and advanced model optimization, gated by verified core pipeline.

Parallelize disjoint media variants, independent test corpus generation and target adapters once underlying contracts are stable. Serialize conflicting schema/root/source writer changes. A draft PR containing enormous mirrored AI-tree changes should not be blindly overlaid onto another feature branch. Each work batch returns exact source paths, new user-visible capability, negative proof, focused tests, changed/unchanged holds, rollback and independent review. Producing twenty PRs without one integrated playable game is not more complete than producing one verified end-to-end slice.

## 51.3 Explicit blockers and promotion math

Four truthful work outcomes: implemented and qualified; implemented but missing target proof; blocked by a concrete reproducible failure; already implemented/duplicate and mapped to the right canonical owner. A valid no-op after discovering an existing verified owner is better than inventing a duplicate feature. Blocks must cite a specific failed invariant and minimum safe repair. Promote only source and toolchain identities with exact-head evidence; pass from another head is context, not a final verdict. Track source/code, model, runtime, rights and policy drift independently so reruns are precise rather than pretending all previously completed tests remain valid forever.

# 53. Neural-symbolic original-game design compiler: constraint witnesses, not optimistic prose

**Batch ID:** FRONTIER-53 | **Lead:** BOT-05 and BOT-07 | **Partners:** BOT-03, BOT-04, BOT-06, BOT-09, BOT-12 | **Existing anchors:** skeleton/forge/game_design_spec.py, skeleton/forge/game_frontier_studio_document.py, skeleton/ai/game_builder/advanced_procedural_world_planner.py, skeleton/ai/game_builder/advanced_procedural_world_runtime.py, skeleton/game/generation/original_world_tenfold_compiler.py and the bounded editor/quest generators.

**Source-derived qualification note:** original_world_tenfold_compiler.py reports 1,024,000 spatial foundations and 12,288,000 composed configurations, explicitly calling itself a bounded topological reference runtime. Those are addressable design configurations, not twelve million separately played, attractive or native-certified games. The frontier objective is to **prove difficult design properties on selected generated instances and ship them in a real player-controlled target**, not merely raise combinatorial counts. Existing canonical project and generator owners retain all state authority; the neural-symbolic layer is an admitted design/validation strategy within them.

## 53.1 Formalize a game as a typed transition system

For an admitted bounded gameplay slice, define a semantic tuple: entity registry E, world/topology graph G, player action grammar A, initial state s0, transition function T(s,a), observation function O(s), constraints C, resource invariants R, terminal predicate W, failure/recovery predicate F, and a versioned RNG policy P. Project-specific designers author E/G/A/C/W/F through the established editor schemas; a generative model can propose candidate descriptions, but only the deterministic parser/validator can materialize executable rule types. This boundary prevents an LLM's fantasy prose from silently becoming game behavior.

Separate **hard constraints**, **user preferences**, **mechanical affordances**, and **presentation constraints**. Hard constraints include property ownership, type-safety, stable source IDs, valid target capabilities, reachable mandatory objectives, bounded resource consumption, no unauthorized cross-scene teleport, rights clearance and save-migration compatibility. Preferences include atmospheric tone, challenge, surprise and art style. Mechanical affordances describe which player verbs are physically expressible by the selected controller and engine. Presentation constraints require sufficient signals that players can perceive state-changing actions; a formally solvable puzzle with an invisible required switch is not playable quality.

Each rule has immutable identity, origin, revision, owner, allowed mutation footprint and proof obligations. Quantities carry units and bounded ranges; coordinate transforms declare frame; inventories enforce nonnegative integer or strictly defined decimal semantics; rule priorities specify deterministic conflict order. Unsupported target semantics produce compile-time diagnostics rather than a silent loss of fidelity. Keep a boundary between proof-oriented logical abstraction and actual physical engine behavior: a navigation witness in a discretized graph is necessary for many puzzles but not sufficient to show collision and locomotion feasibility in Godot.

## 53.2 Design proposal → declarative solver input → witness

The model first emits a schema-constrained, reviewable **DesignCandidate** with rule IDs, constraints, objectives, choices, expected events and target. The constraint compiler deterministically lowers only admitted portions into a bounded solver representation. Candidate techniques include shortest-path or strongly connected component analysis for topology, finite-domain CP-SAT for tile placement and resources, SMT for small typed arithmetic/ordering rules, temporal-logic model checking for mandatory quest progression and symbolic planning for precondition/effect sequences. None should become an unconditional heavyweight dependency; select the smallest justified solver and respect source/toolchain licensing and finite CPU/memory budgets.

A solver result is not merely yes/no. **SAT** requires a witness: ordered actions, initial conditions, consumed resources, intermediate logical states and reached terminal predicate. **UNSAT** requires an inspectable conflict core or an independently checked reason to the extent supported by the solver; a model-authored explanation alone is not a proof. **UNKNOWN/TIMEOUT** is not satisfiable, and the producer must not silently relax requirements. Record the precise abstraction scope: time horizon, maximum state count, hidden variables, randomized transition policy, solver binary identity and optional assumptions. For negative results without a formal unsat core, produce minimized counterexample or bounded search exhaustion evidence, explicitly not a global impossibility proof.

Example constrained dungeon: five rooms; the player can interact with a locked northern door only after collecting one of two valid keys; a potion can sustain a poisonous corridor; combat is optional but dangerous; and at least two player approaches reach a real end condition. Prove that every required item is obtainable before its consuming edge, no generated room blocks the exit, and mandatory combat does not require more health than achievable under declared mechanics. Then compile and play both paths in the target engine. A graph witness that passes through an inaccessible platform is rejected by the physical driver even if its symbolic sequence is valid.

## 53.3 Counterexample-guided iterative synthesis (CEGIS)

Use a bounded **propose → validate → counterexample → minimal revise → validate** loop. The model generates candidate gameplay structure; deterministic analyzers find contradictions, unreachable objectives, unsafe prerequisites or unsupported target operations; the system returns a *small, source-anchored* counterexample with exact rule IDs. The repair proposal must address the counterexample without violating previously established invariants. The loop is limited by ResourceBudget, repair count and diminishing expected value. Avoid unrestricted backtracking that rewrites the whole game every time a single door condition is wrong.

Maintain a **constraint provenance map**: user hard requirement, inferred default, licensed source, engine limitation, explicit human override or generated design choice. When UNSAT, preferentially revise low-authority inferred defaults; preserve user requirements unless the user approves changes. A model cannot make an impossible quest "solvable" by adding an unseen infinite key or disabling damage without recording that design change. Ask human approval for any relaxation that materially changes player goals, difficulty class or story causality. Accepted edits produce new source revisions and invalidate precise dependent witnesses, rather than clearing an entire library or pretending the old proof still applies.

Counterexample minimization should identify the smallest rule set or shortest action sequence that reproduces a failure. Use solver-native unsat cores where available, delta-debugging where not, and replay the result through a separately implemented evaluator. Store genuine minimized failures in a held-out corpus; do not train a candidate on the same examples and immediately claim generalization. The model may propose a "repair" to the tester, but cannot mutate the oracle.

## 53.4 Narrative, economy and physics solver domains

**Narrative:** prove branch reachability, prerequisites, mutually exclusive choices, irreversible consequences, essential NPC survival or alternatives, bounded quest completion and at least two genuinely distinct endings. Represent a story choice as a state-affecting transition; alternative prose alone is not a different ending. A generative story director can optimize drama while preserving consistency of player knowledge and world chronology.

**Economy:** check source/sink conservation, maximum exploit loops, crafting component feasibility, price bounds, idempotent purchase and ownership rules, and resource availability for mandatory progression. Use integer inventories or exact decimals per existing game semantics. Do not grant a key item twice on reload to solve a progression dead end. Permit non-conservative magic systems only when explicit source/sink rules explain them.

**Movement:** derive traversal constraints from actual target controller motion, collision geometry, jump envelope, slope friction and platform timing. A pure graph solver is a prefilter; the final feasibility witness must be checked against engine-implemented actions, including analog gamepad and accessible alternatives. Support variable physics time steps by declaring tolerance and authoritative event endpoints.

**World simulation:** verify region transitions, stable NPC identities, resource transfer, faction/rumor causality and compatible save serialization after time skips. The solver need not enumerate every long-term world state; specify bounded assumptions, symbolic abstractions and property-based campaigns covering far-field aggregate transitions.

## 53.5 Incremental proof invalidation and explainability

A proof is keyed by the exact project source revision, semantic node dependencies, solver/verification version, target runtime physics profile, constraint policy and RNG scheme. A palette edit should not invalidate mandatory quest solvability unless it affects a gameplay cue or accessibility requirement. A jump-height change invalidates route proofs that rely on jump reachability but not a separate dialogue-only graph. A source-rights withdrawal invalidates affected eligible exports independent of logical solvability. An updated game engine may invalidate physical witness tolerances even when symbolic rules are unchanged.

Provide a developer-visible **why-valid/why-invalid** report: accepted user requirements; solver abstraction; witness actions; covered essential paths; unsolved constraints; dependent source nodes; next exact test; and expected mutation surface. Reports must distinguish "proved under this finite abstraction" from "tested on the native engine" and "approved as enjoyable by players". Expose machine-readable evidence for BOT-12 and a human explanation for BOT-11 without allowing free-form model text to forge the verifier's verdict.

## 53.6 Deep acceptance suite

Construct five adversarial design fixtures: (1) physically unreachable jump with an apparently valid room graph; (2) key placed behind its own locked door; (3) quest reward awarded twice through two competing event paths; (4) a required NPC whose death creates an unavoidable softlock; (5) a generated level whose navigation witness disappears after a human edits collision. Add a sixth nonnegative case: two valid story endings with independent real-play traces. The suite fails if the solver claims SAT on invalid states, the compiler silently alters a hard requirement, an UNKNOWN is promoted, a cache reuses stale physics proof, or an actual exported game cannot replay the accepted witness.

**Exit:** one end-to-end generated scenario, human-editable through current project authority, with solver proof, Godot executable, independent input trace and game-save continuation. Then extend the constrained domain family; don't inflate the catalog before a real vertical slice exists.

# 54. Real-time adaptive game direction: causal control, fairness and narrative dramaturgy

**Batch:** FRONTIER-54 | **Lead:** BOT-06 | **Partners:** BOT-05 authoring, BOT-03 offline AI, BOT-04 orchestration, BOT-08 media, BOT-12 evaluation. **Existing anchors:** advanced_quest_director_runtime.py, advanced_gameplay_runtime.py, skeleton/forge/world_events_v1, skeleton/ai/game_builder/director_capability_graph.py and the game-learning paths.

The repository's director_capability_graph.py already declares finite DeviceTier budgets (retro, handheld, mobile, desktop, high_end), a registered dependency graph and a clear disclaimer that an implemented adapter does not grant external permissions or prove proprietary engine integration. Preserve those semantics. The requested advance is not a second privileged real-time AI scheduler. It is a **game-owned, deterministic, player-fair encounter and narrative director** using existing engine capabilities, with slower AI advisers confined to asynchronous bounded proposals. Creative direction must never require a network round trip inside the player's critical frame loop.

## 54.1 Control loop and authoritative actuators

Build a fixed-cadence director that reads bounded **observables**: player progress, objective states, resource levels, recent damage, repeated failures, input skill hints, navigation confusion signals, pacing, visibility/audibility of threats, current NPC/faction rules and local performance pressure. Its admissible **actuators** are explicitly designed game variables such as enemy spawn mix, optional hint timing, ambient intensity, patrol aggression within authored bounds, checkpoint support, music tension or optional event order. It cannot secretly change awarded currency, invalidate a prior player choice, forge a win, teleport an item or change rights/policy.

Define **hard invariants** before optimization: mandatory path remains reachable; current quest prerequisites remain valid; no unfair unavoidable attack is inserted without a declared mechanic; player-selected difficulty/accessibility ceiling is preserved; spawned enemies have a valid collision/navigation location; frame/CPU/audio budgets remain bounded. For deterministic replay, director action proposals become typed events with policy version, observations, seed and accepted decision. Replay uses recorded accepted decisions, not an unrepeatable new model call.

A rational director separates state estimation from action selection. A short-term detector identifies repeated failure or excessive ease using robust evidence windows rather than reacting to one hit. A medium-term policy adjusts pacing while respecting cooldown and hysteresis. A long-term story planner may propose optional plot beats between scenes and requires a validity check against the world-canon graph. No one layer may override a committed user action.

## 54.2 Player modeling and concept drift

Player estimates are **local task observations**, not diagnoses about a real person. Useful dimensions: command fluency, hazard recognition, optional exploration frequency, reaction-time distribution for the game, repeated-route loops, apparent preference for stealth versus direct combat, tutorial completion and whether accessible alternatives are activated. Store only necessary project/session-scoped signals under current governance and retention. Avoid inferring health, protected traits or personality labels. Allow players to disable adaptive challenge and inspect major gameplay adaptations.

Use calibrated uncertainty intervals and minimum sample counts. A novice may intentionally experiment and an expert may roleplay incompetence; a single failed room cannot permanently downgrade difficulty. Maintain a counterfactual baseline: what would the unadapted policy have spawned? Evaluate whether adaptations genuinely improve comprehension/engagement without decreasing player autonomy. Record activation reasons in a bounded developer-facing director trace. Expose user-friendly explanations for meaningful difficulty or hint changes.

## 54.3 Fairness-preserving encounter pacing

For a multi-room action-adventure, build a phase model **anticipation → encounter → peak → recovery → exploration → reveal** with authored optional variations. A pressure estimator combines recent combat intensity, current health/resources, environmental hazards, time since last checkpoint and win/loss history. The director uses finite, constraint-checked action choices with a cooldown to avoid oscillation. Audio/lighting may convey pressure but cannot substitute for an actual gameplay transition. A generated boss phase must give a perceivable telegraph, legitimate defensive response and bounded resource demand.

Define "no unfair surprise" operationally: every unavoidable damage source needs a demonstrated response window under the declared device/control accessibility profile, or a safe alternative. If the current scene is unplayable because of a known geometry bug, the director must not attempt to hide it with easier enemies and claim a quality improvement; escalate a deterministic repair ticket.

## 54.4 Async LLM advisor without game-loop dependency

An admitted Jeeves model can suggest encounter variants, hints, NPC lines, camera cues or optional world events from a **redacted, bounded and source-versioned** snapshot. The response is a proposal only. A deterministic compiler validates schema and source revision; safety/rights and user policy apply; accepted actions are queued for a safe tick boundary or future scene. If the model is slow, cancelled, offline, out of tokens or wrong about the game, the director continues via authored deterministic policy. Speculative LLM text never becomes a privileged rule script at runtime.

This separation allows richer creative behavior without making player input depend on GPU-heavy inference. Record proposal provenance and renderer/audio dependencies; the world source revision change fences stale suggestions. Never allow a model to call a restricted tool on behalf of an NPC simply because the narrative asks it to.

## 54.5 Controlled experiments and quality proof

Run identical source, seed, player policy and hardware profile under **director disabled**, **bounded deterministic director**, and **AI-advised bounded director**. Pre-register completion, unfair damage, softlocks, game-state drift, player comprehension, accessibility, time-to-goal, frame spikes and fun/novelty review. Randomize experimental order and collect multiple runs. Optimize Pareto-safely; a mean satisfaction improvement does not excuse any newly introduced mandatory softlock, privilege leak or catastrophic performance regression.

Negative tests: alternating rapid win/loss causes no difficulty oscillation; pausing never accidentally advances encounter schedule; save/restart doesn't double-spawn unique enemies; model outage leaves combat functional; source revision drift denies proposal; missing audio does not hide mandatory attack cue; an accessibility route stays solvable after adaptation; replay of accepted events is stable. Publish an independent tester video/input trace for at least one adaptive encounter, not only source metrics.

# 55. High-fidelity character foundry: identity, geometry, motion and expression

**Batch:** FRONTIER-55 | **Lead:** BOT-08 | **Partners:** BOT-05 canon/story, BOT-06 physics/runtime, BOT-03 admitted media, BOT-09 export, BOT-11 editors, BOT-12 visual proof. **Existing anchors:** skeleton/ai/game_builder/advanced_animation_runtime.py, advanced_engine_bindings.py, skeleton/forge/game_frontier_studio.py, frontend/src/features/Jeeves/GameFrontierAuthoringPanel.tsx and character generation facades pointing into actual shared cores.

advanced_animation_runtime.py is explicitly a finite animation state and root-motion reference; it does not render skinned bone meshes or import foreign rigs. A high-fidelity character builder must link that proven logical state to actual geometry and rendered behavior, while preserving human editability, platform budgets, rights and character continuity.

## 55.1 Canonical character identity without overfitting to text prompts

A character contains a stable original identity, project ownership, age-appropriate role where relevant, narrative canon, faction, silhouette proportions, high-level facial/garment motifs, color and material palette, expression vocabulary, articulation rig, voice policy and permitted authored variations. The **CharacterBible** is a versioned concept grouping under the established project/canon authority, not an independent celebrity/identity database. Human-authored choices and project lore are high priority; a model should not drift hair, outfit identity or facial landmarks when generating a new pose. Each reference is source/rights reviewed and traceable.

Represent variation with constrained parameters and a stable base identity: view, pose, lighting, costume layer, damage state, seasonal garment, emotion, weather and LOD. A random seed without explicit semantic controls is inadequate for consistency. Distinguish intentional in-world change (aging, injury, changed armor) from accidental output drift. Approval of a new appearance creates a canon revision and invalidates only dependent assets. The user can lock silhouette, palette, anatomy, emblem, and face markers at different levels of strictness.

Do not claim likeness, voice or appearance rights from a generated output alone. A real person's identifiable reference image or voice sample requires appropriate permission and processing scope. Original fictional voice identities must be checked for consent and rights where applicable, with revocation and alternative voice/caption routes. When external image and audio providers are not installed, build from lawful user-supplied or procedural source and mark unavailable generative features honestly.

## 55.2 3D mesh and rig validation sequence

Pipeline: **design → base mesh → topology/UV/material → rig hierarchy → skin weights → authored motion → retarget → physics/contact → engine import → actual runtime capture → target LOD/export**. The source artifact is not erased when creating a target-specific optimized derivative. Require mesh unit/up-axis convention, vertex and primitive bounds, manifold/winding checks where required, UV mapping, tangent normals, material channels/colorspace, skeleton joint IDs, parent acyclicity, inverse bind transforms and normalized skin weights. Where automatic rigging fails, retain an editor-correctable diagnostic rather than fabricate a working skeletal mesh.

A runtime skeleton mapping must connect exact authored logical action states to target animation tree and bone transforms. Validate bind-pose compatibility and root hierarchy, disallow zero-length or nonfinite transforms, reject missing mandatory bone mappings and carry semantic attachment points for hands, eyes, hit zones, equipped items and prop sockets. Clip retargeting may require pose correction or proportion-aware IK; test out-of-scale characters and nonhuman rigs with explicit supported profiles rather than assuming all humanoid mappings generalize.

For the player's moves, define root-motion policy: either physics/controller owns root displacement and animation follows, or authorized root motion contributes within collision checks. Never let both accumulate displacement independently. High-speed attacks need correct hitbox synchronization; foot contact should reflect actual ground and avoid perceptible foot skating; ledge traversal must not teleport the collision body through obstacles.

## 55.3 Facial animation, lip sync and emotional continuity

Define expression as authored action parameters, not arbitrary emotion inferred about real users. Blendshape or skeletal face controls map dialogue phonemes/visemes, gaze, eyelid motion and authored expression cues into target frame transforms under bounded magnitudes. Voice output and phoneme alignment use real decodable audio with source/consent; text-only dialogue uses deterministic approximate mouth or subtitle presentation, honestly labeled. A facial expression cannot override a confirmed plot beat or cause an illegal NPC action.

Cinematic shots require robust eye line, pose and speech synchronization; avoid mouth moving during silence, uncontrolled blinking across cuts, geometry clipping and gaze through obstructing objects. Test transitions between a neutral state, surprise, dialogue, pain, locomotion and cinematic close-up. Performance tiers may drop facial detail while preserving required emotional cues and captions.

## 55.4 Cloth, hair, equipment and environment

Soft-body cloth/hair simulation should be optional and bounded by target hardware. Design deterministic or repeatable fallback rigged motion for mobile/retro/CPU-only targets. Simulated garments are constrained by skeleton, collisions and authored attachment; changing equipment must preserve item ownership and source license, not spontaneously add in-game inventory. Weather/wind may affect material presentation while maintaining game-level collision and quest consistency.

Asset constraints: helmet clips not through hair, weapon grip targets match the rig, capes do not obscure mandatory visual cues, footwear/terrain contacts remain readable, facial shading stable under light changes and LOD collapse avoids dropping the essential quest indicator. Consider physics delta scaling, material reflections, hair transparency/alpha sorting and skin-tone gamut compatibility without overfitting to one reference capture. Adaptive LOD uses actual measured frame cost and user settings; do not use speculative "neural rendering" if unavailable in the target engine.

## 55.5 2D animation consistency

For pixel or 2D vector games, preserve character identity across directions, frames, motion poses, facial variants, palette swaps and UI portraits. A sprite atlas needs stable pivot/scale, collision/hitbox synchronization and frame order. Validate UV padding and gutters to prevent tile bleeding, alpha/premultiplication artifacts, animation event alignment and pixel-grid behavior. Procedural animation may blend skeletal 2D joints with frame animation where the target supports it, but the same logical gameplay action must have one authoritative event interpretation.

Any generative inpainting/variation step retains original image, region mask, model settings and rights chain. A tool should not alter the whole sprite when the artist approved only a hand adjustment. Human fine-tuning and version comparison must remain available when AI media is disabled.

## 55.6 Character acceptance suite on real gameplay

Create one small, originally authored character with at least idle, walk, run, jump, land, attack, hurt and interaction states; one equipment change and one dialogue gesture. Bind authored rig/animation actions into a real Godot target; record controller inputs, root/collision state and frames; verify item sockets, visual state, clip timing, game hit event and pause/save/resume. Inject missing bone, malformed skin weights, incompatible retarget, broken hitbox alignment, corrupt texture, unauthorized voice asset and unsupported shader; these must fail at the correct gate. Repeat on at least two different target performance profiles where those profiles are claimed supported.
