**Exit:** not merely "character generated" but a real, playable, consistent character with source-editable identity and capture-backed motion/rights receipts. Character variety can scale only after consistency and reuse controls pass.

# 56. Autonomous gameplay debugger: causal fault localization and minimal verified repair

**Batch:** FRONTIER-56 | **Lead:** BOT-06 + BOT-04 | **Independent tester:** BOT-12 | **Sources:** skeleton/forge/repair.py, skeleton/forge/godot_emit.py, skeleton/forge/playtest.py, skeleton/jeeves/game_comparison_counterfactual.py and actual game studio clients.

The existing forge repair scaffold is policy gated and bounded. The existing playtest gate actually boots Godot headlessly. The existing counterfactual comparison path documents bounded controlled-input experiments over independently approved native game workers. Build on these legitimate primitives. The next frontier is **repairing a reproducible game behavior failure from actual engine evidence, changing the smallest authoritative source rule, and rerunning independent play**, not automatically rewriting an exporter to make a static test pass.

## 56.1 Observability substrate and bug dossier

A bug is a concrete trace: user-visible symptom; source/game revision and package hash; engine/toolchain version; initial game save; seed and RNG policy; controller events including press/hold/release; relevant world event identifiers; scene/input/animation state; frame/audio capture references; server/editor/engine logs; hardware/OS profile; first observed mismatch and expected invariant. The dossier is attached to the existing issue/project operation; it does not create a new autonomous bug database. Sensitive user data is redacted and retention follows governance policy.

Avoid collecting unlimited video, private filesystem paths or entire model contexts. Store bounded, content-addressed segments with source scope and event intervals. If reproduction depends on a host race, record the uncertain timing and attempt controlled reruns; do not counterfeit deterministic exactness. Distinguish an engine crash from a dead-end quest, perceptual invisibility, bad UI input mapping or network projection delay. Test assertions must refer to actual observed behavior rather than a model's preferred narrative.

## 56.2 Causal localization through dependency and counterfactuals

First classify the failure: design constraint, semantic state transition, exporter mapping, engine script/signal, collision/physics, asset/renderer, audiovisual synchronization, saved-state migration, UI projection, target packaging or environmental/toolchain defect. Use the source-to-engine provenance graph to reduce scope to candidate rule IDs and files. The verifier can replay a held-out trace at parent/candidate revisions and compare divergence tick and affected state. A binary search through changed project revisions is useful only when a stable reproducer exists and the dependency graph supports it.

Counterfactual actions: replace one controller event, change one scene rule under an isolated test revision, disable a single optional asset cue, rerun with a known-good engine build, or swap only a source/target adapter. The objective is to isolate a necessary/sufficient causal factor while minimizing unrelated mutations. Confounded experiments (different hardware, policy, toolchain and seed simultaneously) cannot establish cause; keep variables pinned or report inconclusive. A model can rank hypotheses, but evidence from actually executed alternatives determines validity.

When bisecting exported artifacts, compare their actual executable digests. A compiler log from one game package cannot prove another package's behavior. A stale frontend frame may be a transport or cache bug; don't "fix" gameplay logic merely to satisfy the UI.

## 56.3 Repair proposal as a typed, reversible mutation

A repair proposal binds failure dossier, source parent digest, changed semantic nodes or exact code files, preconditions, expected behavior and regression set. It declares whether the patch is a game-design revision, emitter/adapter change or canonical product code change. Only allowed tool scopes can apply it; generated arbitrary code must be scanned and sandboxed. The agent cannot modify the test oracle, remove the requirement, suppress engine logs or expand timeouts indefinitely as a "fix". It cannot permanently relax safety, rights or trust policy to get green checks.

Prefer the **smallest semantic fix** measured by affected dependency closure, not necessarily fewest text lines. Repairing a missing collision signal may involve one script and one scene import plus a test; copying the entire canonical emitted scaffold may be safe in some known cases but must not erase user modifications. Compare an upstream emitter fix to a one-off game patch; repair the correct owner so future generated games inherit the behavior when appropriate.

Bound iterative attempts, build minutes, model tokens, changed files, generated assets and number of failed or inconclusive tests. Preserve all accepted project revisions and reversible artifacts; on exhaustion return the known failure and a partial proposed diff, not an invented success state.

## 56.4 Independent repair verifier and mutation testing

Require the originally failing trace to fail on the parent, pass on the repaired candidate, and remain stable across independently selected seeds or representative neighboring scenarios. Add negative regression checks for adjacent mechanics and human-approved behaviors. Mutation testing intentionally reintroduces the defect, disables one engine signal, changes a quest reward or removes a collision mapping; the test suite must then fail. If the result still passes after removing the feature, it is not a genuine verification of that feature.

For flaky outcomes, run a pre-registered repeat plan and classify unstable environment versus nondeterministic bug. Record false-positive rate and regression scope; avoid model self-scoring. A high-confidence repair can still require human review if it changes gameplay difficulty, narrative causality, source ownership or commercial release behavior. Each accepted repair creates a new source/project revision, invalidating affected exact-head and game evidence.

## 56.5 Browser/editor and native debugging trace linkage

The existing GamePlayViewport can send authenticated inputs and display server-side game frames; the toolchain also supports exported Godot artifacts. Keep distinct test identities for the two runtimes and provide a debugging bridge rather than assuming their frames are equivalent. Show a source-time timeline of player inputs, world event commits, editor transformations and engine frames. A human can jump to the first divergent tick, highlight a source rule and inspect candidate patch with clear before/after behavior. A bug report initiated from the UI must not gain permission to read a different project or run unrestricted tools.

## 56.6 Exit campaign

Take three real seeded failures: one unreachable platform/door, one duplicated reward on save/replay and one missing audiovisual action cue. Reproduce each using a real game/input driver; locate a causal source; apply bounded repair to the canonical owner; rerun headless import, interactive play, save/restart and clean-target build. At least one test must be able to fail if the candidate reverts to the old bug. Preserve a candidate failure if the repaired game is not independently winnable. Release holds remain until exact-head target proof succeeds.

# 57. Cross-platform playable compiler: lawful targets, native performance and clean-room evidence

**Batch:** FRONTIER-57 | **Lead:** BOT-09 | **Partners:** BOT-01, BOT-02, BOT-05, BOT-06, BOT-08, BOT-12. **Source anchors:** skeleton/ai/game_builder/desktop_native_export.py, dual_runtime_export.py, skeleton/forge/godot_emit.py, skeleton/forge/playtest.py, skeleton/jeeves/game_console_build.py, skeleton/jeeves/game_desktop_export.py and existing distinct genre-specific Godot adapters.

desktop_native_export.py explicitly produces C11/SDL2 sources, CMake and a sealed manifest for original games while disclaiming compiler, runtime, installer, signing keys or runnable .exe presence. This is a valid source-delivery feature, not a contradiction; the next step is to build and test actual outputs on declared targets. Do not discard this original native path merely to claim everything is Godot, and do not equate any source emitter with a tested executable.

## 57.1 Target capability algebra

Treat target support as a **typed set of guarantees**, not a marketing label. A target profile includes machine architecture, OS/version, runtime/engine version and digest, script/code language, input devices, graphics/audio capability, storage/save semantics, memory/frame ceilings, rights/licensing constraints, package/export format, executable signing and clean-runner proof. The source game IR declares required capabilities. Build admissibility computes an explicit compatibility relation: a game is eligible only when every required semantic operation is supported by the target (or the user has approved a specific semantics-preserving degradation with new acceptance). Generic "works on mobile" is not meaningful without declared touch UI, asset budgets, sandbox and hardware evidence.

Separate platform-independent gameplay rules from target-specific input/render/packaging. A 2D browser maze, an SDL2 desktop maze, a Godot 3D RPG and lawful retro/homebrew source target may share objective/inventory/quest notions but require distinct native drivers. Portable behavior must be proven per game+target, not inferred from sibling build success. A valid output declares one or more supported targets and can honestly reject others.

## 57.2 Deterministic lowering and build manifest

Each admitted build records exact game source revision, semantic IR digest, compiler/emitter version, game rules, dependencies and rights, target SDK/engine digest, selected features, generated paths, build environment and output digest. Lowering produces editable target source and independent target manifest. Generated executable code cannot receive production service credentials or unrestricted network access; the build runner operates within an admitted sandbox and finite CPU/RAM/disk/time. Active-content scanning applies to generated game scripts and binaries as appropriate.

Where reproducibility is feasible, compare byte-for-byte outputs from fixed inputs and pinned toolchain. Where nondeterministic build metadata or native linking prevents bitwise equality, declare the expected variation and require semantic/gameplay parity plus provenance equivalence. Build artifacts use atomic staging and publication, with backup/rollback; an interrupted compiler cannot overwrite the previous successfully tested package. A fresh target runner should launch without access to development checkout source.

## 57.3 Godot production path

Inventory existing puzzle/racing/platformer/shooter/farming/survival/tactics/defense/other Godot adapters and map each to a target feature/genre matrix. For each claimed supported genre, run import, parse, real scene boot, controller-to-gameplay trace, save/restart, media proof, native export templates and clean target launch. The existing headless gate is the starting proof for engine boot, not final completion. Verify input maps, scene node references, autoload identity, graphics/audio import, collision and exported resource paths against the engine version actually shipped.

On Windows and Linux, distinguish host-native binaries from running a headless engine inside a container. On mobile, require actual platform build, touch/controller behavior and device constraints; do not infer mobile from shared source. Browser Godot/WebGL paths require separate asset/network/browser storage and CPU/GPU proof. Unsupported engine features must return actionable errors rather than silently strip required gameplay.

## 57.4 C11/SDL2 native path

For original source-driven games, use the existing CMake + SDL2 project and verify an actual available compiler, SDK, runtime link, input event path and platform package. Portable core rules can be cross-checked against the semantic reference test but must be executed in the native binary. Test controlled keyboard/gamepad input, frame state, collision/win/retry, save path, clean install and asset decoding. Packaging must include redistributable libraries with legitimate licenses and target architecture. A compilation success on one Linux CI container does not prove a Windows .exe or macOS app was produced.

If an SDK is unavailable, return source-only artifact status with a toolchain report. Do not synthesize fake executable names or claim build performance from source language. A "dual runtime" manifest means two independently verified targets only after each target is compiled and played; a single shared receipt cannot certify both.

## 57.5 Retro/homebrew legality and device constraints

Retro and pre-2000 target profiles must preserve legal provenance: independently licensed toolchains, original game content, no unlicensed BIOS/ROM extraction or proprietary SDK bypass, explicit emulator/hardware identity and per-target limits. Static source generation for a platform is not proof that approved hardware or a legitimate emulator can run it. Different targets have incompatible display resolution, palette, input timing, audio channels, memory, cartridge/save layout and CPU scheduling; enforce constraints before export.

Build a **legal-original-game target matrix** for source, compiled image, emulator boot, input-driven play, native hardware and distributable package with separate evidence. When an actual toolchain/device is unavailable, retain source delivery and mark executable/device proof absent. Tests on game inspiration or public domain materials do not grant permission to reuse third-party games as commercial assets.

## 57.6 Full publication receipt

A release candidate carries: source SHA and project revision, target profile, engine/toolchain bytes, build outputs and digests, media/source rights, SBOM, dependency/license scan, malware gate status, playable end-state trace, save-schema compatibility, performance profile, human approval, rollback and support limitations. No agent or PR description can waive a missing gate. An original game may be usable offline without storefront integration, but public commercial distribution requires extra entitlement, signing and legal decisions.

**Exit case:** one original game is both playable and editable in source, tested in actual Godot on a declared desktop target, and separately compiled/played under SDL2 if dual-target support is claimed. Show clean-host launch and player completion. Record any nonqualified targets explicitly. Additional genres can be promoted one at a time based on the same evidence chain.

# 58. Protected game learning and model promotion: from actual gameplay to better game creation

**Work packet:** FRONTIER-58 | **Lead:** BOT-03 | **Co-leads:** BOT-04 orchestration, BOT-06 play, BOT-10 legal evidence, BOT-12 independent evaluation | **Status:** PROPOSED qualification/connection work, not evidence of any deployed new weights.

**Observed source anchors:** skeleton/ai/game_builder/game_model_promotion.py, game_reviewer_optimizer.py, game_18round_evolution.py, game_18round_runtime.py, game_18round_shadow_sandbox.py, game_training_flow.py and skeleton/jeeves/game_learning.py. The existing model-promotion path describes a real input-feature *classifier*, not an LLM; the optimizer selects on TRAIN/VALIDATION and limits TEST to the frozen winner. The 18-round journal is candid that its receipts do not prove live inference, crawling, new data or actual weight training. Preserve this crucial separation: advisory game-reviewer or policy adaptation is not proof of improved foundational GGUF parameters.

## 58.1 Declare distinct learning lanes and their authorities

**Lane A — Gameplay policy learning.** Learn a bounded policy that chooses finite actions for a real, explicitly versioned game environment. Inputs include game artifact digest, controller schema, initial save, action/observation history, rewards, termination and allowed experiment budget. The owner is the existing game-learning runtime. Output can be a tested navigation/agent policy, but a successful policy has not necessarily learned how to write games, passed a physical native test, or fine-tuned a language model.

**Lane B — Defect and quality reviewer learning.** Train a calibrated classifier on independently labelled gameplay traces, design/asset/rights evidence and known bugs. Its output helps choose which projects deserve further playtest. It cannot replace actual engine execution or certify release. Use per-family false-green rates: a reviewer that recognizes many cosmetic issues but misses one critical save-corruption family is inappropriate for critical decision authority even if aggregate accuracy rises.

**Lane C — Optional local model-weight adaptation.** Actual changes to a language/vision/audio model must use the canonical provider/training owner, admitted hardware and model bytes, rightfully collected data, frozen independent tests, staged/rollback artifacts, and explicit activation authority. A "hyperweight" or shadow reviewer-policy reference is not a new LLM checkpoint. The training system must refuse to infer training completed merely because a signed round was appended.

Every lane uses its actual existing schema and persistence owner; names in this chapter are design categories, not authorization to create another learner database or privileged agent hierarchy.

## 58.2 Training-data custody and partition strategy

A project-derived training example contains source project/revision, origin and allowed use, initial game state, relevant input trace, target engine version, true observed result, human or independent oracle label, and content digest. Split by game *lineage*, not by row: color variants, rewrites, remixes or procedural seeds of the same mission cannot be allowed to leak from TRAIN to TEST. Genre and engine coverage are reported separately, and a long corpus of tiny maze variants cannot certify a 3D role-playing game reviewer.

Protect user-owned source and media under existing governance. A publicly readable source is not automatic commercial reuse or model-training permission. A Dragon research summary marked research-only cannot become gradient data. Any applicable consent, licenses, retention, withdrawal and data-class constraints follow samples into datasets, derived model candidates and evaluation artifacts. If retroactive machine unlearning cannot be established, describe the real containment/retirement behavior instead of claiming exact deletion from learned parameters.

For critical labels, use actual reproducible evidence. Examples include unreachable objectives, duplicate item grant, stale project state, collision mismatch, broken action bindings, frame stalls, misleading tutorial, inaccessible cues, script import failure, unplayable export, corrupted save and unauthorized source asset. Synthetic examples help cover corners, but should not replace varied actual games and human annotations for subjective quality.

## 58.3 Frozen evaluation and calibrated abstention

Pre-register feature extraction, baseline champion, candidate class, training budget, hyperparameters, seed, partition digests, critical defect taxonomy, uncertainty threshold and qualified use cases. The candidate search may inspect only TRAIN and VALIDATION; sealed TEST is revealed to the frozen selected model under the current promotion contract. Existing PromotionStandard already expresses bounded accuracy, critical recall, calibration, generalization and regression controls—respect the active file, do not rewrite the policy after seeing outcomes.

Use project-level and defect-family confusion matrices, confidence intervals, precision/recall for critical defects, calibration/Brier score, abstention rates and out-of-domain labels. A review model that is uncertain about an unknown genre should abstain rather than give confident green. New evaluation evidence must bind exact model/feature extractor, project source, tester, scorer, toolchain and dataset. If a model or rubric changes, expire the affected verdicts.

Stage reviewers in shadow mode first. Compare frozen candidate to current champion on newly produced games and independent play traces without granting live mutation or release rights. Champion rollback must be a finite, tested decision. No classifier output grants new capability, tool access, tenant access, source rights or model-provider weight activation.

## 58.4 Eighteen-round evolution, source-grounded physical effects

Partition rounds by effect type: planning/priority; deterministic data transformation; sandbox computation; actual admitted inference; actual rights-approved network capture; actual authorized training; native game execution; human approval; active promotion. A signed journal event establishes only its own custody. To claim a real external effect, require the corresponding physical tool/network/engine/model receipt, with operation identity and current authorization. This prevents a multi-step reasoning chain from being interpreted as independent actual work.

An optimization round can propose better replay seeding, counterexample selection, probability ordering or model routing and still be a valuable planning result. It is not a training run until a trusted process used real training data and produced real checkpoint bytes. It is not crawl evidence without transport/capture records. It is not quality superiority without held-out comparisons. Respect existing idle, thermal, privacy and source-license conditions and do not activate new weights behind an operator's back.

## 58.5 Learning must improve a playable user journey

Close the loop: capture a real bug or design weakness; derive valid label and minimal trace; suggest a bounded project/tool mutation; create a new candidate project revision; run actual engine tests; compare gameplay on held-out inputs; let a human and deterministic gates accept or reject. The verifier must detect score gaming such as removing all enemies, changing the victory predicate or weakening collision to obtain a higher "completion" rate. Preserve test oracle and user's hard requirements. Increasing an advisory classifier's confidence alone is never proof that the game improved.

Mandatory negatives: project lineage leakage; revoked training consent; fabricated labelled trace; hyperparameter selection on TEST; missing tokenizer/model identity; shadow proposal attempting real release; tenant-crossing dataset join; promotion after a source-policy change; optimizer that degrades critical bug recall; and replay that double-commits rewards. A real model outage should leave deterministic gameplay operational and make its training/assistant functionality honestly unavailable.

# 59. Epic world streaming and persistent scene identity under bounded hardware

**Work packet:** FRONTIER-59 | **Lead:** BOT-07/BOT-05 | **Partners:** BOT-06 gameplay, BOT-08 rendering, BOT-09 export, BOT-11 editor, BOT-12 acceptance. **Inspected source anchors:** advanced_procedural_world_runtime.py, game_frontier_studio_epic_lod.py, game_frontier_studio_production_recipes.py and game_frontier_studio_epic_route_graph.py. The existing procedural runtime uses integer-coordinate portable terrain with rebuild/save_deltas/snapshot policies; the visual LOD allocator fairly distributes a hard 8192-instance budget without inventing collision/nav geometry. Its controls must be preserved.

## 59.1 Addressable hierarchy without eager massive instantiation

Define stable world → epoch → region → district → scene → chunk → entity identity. Each generated chunk is specified by canonical project/world, integer cell coordinates, terrain-law version, seed/RNG algorithm, approved source assets and locked human-authored overrides. A content-addressed base represents repeatable procedural content. State mutations such as harvested deposits, opened gates, player buildings, faction decisions and NPC memories live as committed events or versioned deltas under the existing game authority, not in a mutable random seed.

The stated hierarchy of 100 chapters / 1000 acts / 9999 scenes is an addressable creative project structure. Each position has an independent maturity state—reserved, authored, composed, compiled, playtested or target-qualified. Empty positions do not count as shipped scenes, and a catalog cardinality does not imply that many independent playable games exist. Lazy generation produces only approved content needed for the current project and target while preserving exact source canon and rights.

Integer world cells should map to local render/physics coordinates via explicit coordinate frames. Moving the floating origin cannot move the canonical actor, change its quest history or duplicate region ownership. Cross-world portals are atomic identity-preserving transfers; if load or policy validation fails, the player remains at a safe authoritative location. A world archive must retain enough source and event data to reconstruct observed player consequences, not all hypothetical untouched terrain.

## 59.2 Simulation fidelity tiers and actor promotion

**Active region:** actual player controls, real physics/collision, nearby NPC decisions, critical quest triggers, audiovisual fidelity and responsive save interactions. **Adjacent region:** lower-frequency AI/nav and prefetch with enough data to preserve nearby impending events. **Remote region:** aggregate deterministic society/economy/time evolution or frozen source snapshot with event cursor.

Promoting an actor remote→active reconstructs the *same* identity, location, inventory, goals, witnessed memory, commitments and causal ancestry, not a newly generated duplicate. Demoting active→remote commits necessary state before freeing expensive physics, GPU or decoded media. Use source revisions and bounded leases so two workers never claim a single region simultaneously. A late remote simulation result cannot overwrite newer active gameplay. Replaying the same seed without accepted events must not replenish mined resources or restore defeated unique enemies.

NPCs do not gain omniscient knowledge simply by moving to a cheaper tier; preserve their observed information and permitted rumor propagation. A distant merchant may pursue a recorded trip through a coarse spatial route, but cannot instantaneously teleport across world regions to make a schedule appear plausible.

## 59.3 Semantics-priority streaming and cost-aware LOD

Streaming priority combines player predicted motion, camera visibility, current quest relevance, active character interactions, collision readiness, navigation, rights validity, source availability and physical capacity. A mission-critical bridge cannot be rendered as traversable before its collision representation is ready. A high-resolution texture may be absent temporarily, but the mandatory clue and accessible cue must remain readable.

Asset readiness stages map through existing build and artifact owners: planned; deriving/importing; validated; simulation-ready; rendering-ready; active; evicting; retained as base+delta. Each transition has finite CPU/RAM/GPU/disk budgets and revocation behavior. Background Jeeves generation cannot consume all available GPU memory and starve a player. Fair-share LOD of multi-layer scenes builds on the actual epic_lod algorithm rather than ignoring its represented-layer guarantee.

Use texture/mesh/animation LOD, bounded GPU upload, asset prefetch, spatial chunk priority and cache eviction, but never alter underlying quest, collision or economy semantics as a side effect of visual simplification. A withdrawn media source invalidates applicable export rights even if the cache still holds rendered bytes.

## 59.4 Procedural variety versus mere combinatorial indexing

The user's "quintillions of variations" ambition must be expressed as a measured design space. The meaningful axes are objective architecture, player verbs, route constraints, NPC/faction causality, progression, environment, encounter pacing, visual style and ending dependencies. A large product of options may contain mechanically near-identical states. Analyze distinct reachable experiences, not just seed count. Validate representative generated projects across held-out seeds with actual engine navigation, resource availability and human quality sampling.

Lock important human-authored worlds and scene identities. Regenerate only affected neighborhoods and re-solve dependent navigation/mission feasibility when a terrain rule changes. If one changed bridge collapses a critical path, the generator must explain the dependency and propose a repair instead of overwriting the human's authored story with a new random quest.

## 59.5 Scene acceptance under real pressure

Create a playable multi-layer world containing surface, cave and elevated sky/vertical sections; at least one named unique NPC, scarce item and quest whose state crosses chunk boundaries. Have the player traverse several regions, harvest, build, save, teleport, restart and return. Assert the same identities, inventories and world event cursor despite cache eviction. Remove one derived chunk cache and prove its regeneration from approved base+committed deltas. Inject a competing lease, partial demotion, source-rights withdrawal and GPU pressure. Record actual frame spikes, memory and streaming latency. A screenshot of 8192 logical instances is not the proof of physical traversability.

# 60. Cinematography and audio: compile commands into real time-aligned media

**Work packet:** FRONTIER-60 | **Lead:** BOT-08 | **Partners:** BOT-05 narrative, BOT-06 engine, BOT-09 export, BOT-11 editor, BOT-12 audiovisual proof. **Observed anchors:** modular_scene_compositor.py explicitly produces a render-command model, not an actual video/audio asset. advanced_audio_runtime.py schedules and ducks source-authored cue state in integer samples without creating sound-card output. Maintain these truthful descriptions and add verified real engine adapters, not inflated capability names.

## 60.1 Multi-clock timeline grammar

A playable cinematic contains canonical scene/revision, actor identities, camera shot path, actor animation action/clip, dialogue/caption cues, soundtrack/FX cue, optional player decision, lighting/environment changes and state-changing postconditions. Distinguish *game logical ticks*, *scene timeline*, *animation-local frames*, *audio sample time* and *wall-clock capture time*. The mapping is explicit; slow motion, pause, scene load, audio device interruption and skipped dialogue cannot be solved by assuming all clocks match.

Events carry identity and idempotency. Replaying a camera move or subtitle is safe; replaying a unique reward is not. The world owner commits actual gameplay consequences, while the scene compositor and mixer are derived presentations. Skipping a cutscene must apply its required authored end state once and release controls. A save during a cutscene resumes at a compatible checkpoint or a declared safe state, not a half-applied reward plus looped camera.

## 60.2 Camera direction as constrained geometry

Shots specify target actor, narrative purpose, frame composition, lens/FOV, acceptable pan/zoom, occlusion/collision rules, safe subtitle region, scene coordinate transform and reduced-motion alternative. A candidate shot generator can optimize visibility and dramatic clarity using geometry-aware search, but must validate with the actual renderer and target screen formats. An over-the-shoulder conversation with the speaking NPC permanently outside frame is a bug even if the numerical camera track is well-formed.

Human editors can lock accepted keyframes and regenerate only surrounding segments. Keep voice, gestures, camera and narrative canon in one versioned timeline but separate runtime source owners. The compiler should emit real target-camera nodes/animations and report missing character/rig/cue dependencies before build. An LLM recommendation about camera beauty is not proof that the exported scene renders.

## 60.3 Real mixer buses, stems and accessible cues

The logical AudioCueState must bind to validated PCM/OGG/WAV or another supported decodable source, mixer bus, sample rate, channels, amplitude, loop, attenuation and rights record. Admitted original music and sound stems may use layered arrangements and dynamic transitions; avoid latency-critical neural synthesis in the gameplay frame loop. Measure audio buffer underruns, clipped levels, subtitle timing and priority ducking under paused and resumed play. If an audio provider is absent, the editor may produce a cue plan but cannot claim actual generated music.

Voice requires source and identity consent. Subtitle-only output remains a valid supported fallback when voice cannot be produced, and essential game information must not depend solely on sound. A mute or reduced-motion setting cannot erase key gameplay choices. Media revocation and edits invalidate downstream render/audio exports by source dependency.

## 60.4 Interactive cinematics and source-to-observation parity

A cutscene with a player branch records the actual input event, allowed choice, game-rule consequence, new scene state, cue changes and save cursor. If the player skips, correct canonical consequences remain. If the player pauses or controller disconnects, no hidden selection is committed. Camera/body transforms and audio cues derive from committed scene state and do not independently grant inventory or alter quest flags.

The studio timeline needs actual preview playback and track editing, including a source-diff view. Test original conversation, one action reveal and two branches through real engine frames, mixer capture or clearly labelled engine-buffer evidence, subtitles and controller transitions. Test skipping before/after the consequence, saving mid-shot, switching locale and restoring after crash. A textual render-command list cannot qualify the video/audio feature.

# 61. Multiplayer and creator collaboration: separate gameplay replication from project authority

**Work packet:** FRONTIER-61 | **Lead:** BOT-06 with BOT-02 | **Partners:** BOT-05, BOT-09, BOT-11, BOT-12. **Observed source boundary:** advanced_engine_bindings.py lists advanced_networking_runtime as an original reference engine module; no such registration alone proves deployed public multiplayer. No new privileged game server is authorized here.

## 61.1 Explicit target profiles

Order support by concrete proof: offline single-player; same-device local co-op; LAN-host-authoritative; asynchronous turn-based; and optional remote hosted play if separately approved. Each target declares actor identity, authoritative world owner, controller/action grammar, tick/turn ordering, event persistence, join/leave, save, disconnect, network permissions, cost, abuse policy and native runner. An exported game's host is not necessarily the app backend, and the source file must not silently create privileged public internet infrastructure.

For local co-op, input binding and player ownership remain separate. For LAN or hosted play, clients submit *intents*, never final inventory rewards or victory decisions. Host validates movement, quest changes and economy under the game rules. A turn-based game may use ordered action log and compare-and-swap; a real-time game may use prediction/interpolation with authoritative rollback/reconciliation. Deterministic lockstep cannot be assumed correct across arbitrary physics/toolchains.

## 61.2 Network action consistency and security

A remote input carries session/principal, source game package identity, sequence, tick, finite payload, bounded timing and replay guard. The authoritative host validates membership, rates, state version, action preconditions and actual effects. Attack cases include packet replay, duplicate join, cheating inventory, reordered attack, disconnect during reward, simultaneous key pickup, split-brain host and client state divergence. A malicious client must not mint unique rewards or overwrite another player's save.

Session chat, user-created assets and multiplayer names have separately scoped privacy/content/rights controls. In-game text is not an administrative tool call. An offline game remains playable when networking is disabled if offline single-player support is part of the target contract. Remote hosted mode must have real service, authenticated deployment and tested recovery, not a local source demo masquerading as a globally available game.

## 61.3 Collaborative authoring uses semantic CAS

Co-authors change one canonical project source through actor grants, versioned proposals, semantic conflict detection and audit. CRDT text can help collaborative descriptions, but it is not independent authority over world events, licensed media or public release. Two users can change different lines that jointly invalidate quest solvability; run the game IR/constraint verifier before commit. A user offline draft re-enters with its original parent revision and must be rebased/reviewed if the canonical project advanced.

Presence indicators and selection cursors are derived UI conveniences. They never disclose private files, cross-tenant source or hidden tool permissions. Changing account or project fences stale async responses and clears previous private preview projections.

## 61.4 Native multiplayer proof

Qualify each mode independently: two real local controllers exercising distinct actors; two LAN clients with observed host authority, disconnect/rejoin and exactly-once rewards; two concurrent turn submissions where only one commits to a given turn; and (only if claimed) physical remote service latency/recovery and rights checks. Input traces, game package digests, host source, state and network faults belong to the evidence. Passing local co-op does not certify online play.

# 62. Autonomous playtest fleet and experimental game-quality observability

**Packet:** FRONTIER-62 | **Owner:** BOT-12 with BOT-06 | **Partners:** BOT-03 policy learning, BOT-04 work scheduling, BOT-05 world graph, BOT-07 generation and BOT-11 visual cockpit | **Status:** additional implementation mandate, not proof of an active real-device playtest fleet.

The existing repository contains bounded simulation, play sessions, game recordings, headless Godot boot, game-emulator comparisons and reviewer learning. The critical frontier gap is proving that these systems can evaluate **what a player actually experiences in the game that Skeleton exports**. Do not build a second evaluation application that merely reads project JSON. A real test agent must use a declared controller interface, observe the actual game and retain a complete source- and target-bound evidence chain.

## 62.1 Player test environment identity

A reproducible test environment has an immutable **EnvironmentSpec** view of existing game/test owners: game package digest; project source revision; engine or emulator version/digest; target OS/architecture; input device mapping; screen/audio capture capabilities; initial save/snapshot; RNG algorithm and seed; frame/tick budget; data-retention policy; and physical hardware profile. The test harness must not launch arbitrary game code on the privileged app backend. It uses sandboxed target execution with bounded CPU, memory, process count, filesystem, artifact bytes, and network denied unless specifically required and authorized.

The environment exposes narrow **observation** and **action** interfaces. Observations may include rendered frames, explicitly instrumented game state available only to independent verifier, audio buffers, controller focus, collision contacts, event traces and terminal conditions. Actions include button press/release, analog controls, pointer/touch events, permitted menu operations, bounded waits and reset to an authenticated checkpoint. A bot may not mark itself victorious through a hidden debug mutation when normal players cannot. Instrumentation is isolated from game code, with a disabled/restricted mode for release comparison.

## 62.2 Diverse tester policies, not one optimized oracle

The fleet should include a script-based deterministic sanity walker; bounded path-search agent; novice exploration behavior; expert/high-precision control; accessibility variants; frustration/backtracking detector; malformed/unexpected input adversary; and a held-out game-winning evaluator. Learning-based tester policies remain optional through the existing model/runtime authority and must not be able to modify the target executable or evaluation rubric. Each policy declares its skill assumptions and acceptable observation access. A privileged omniscient quest solver is useful for *logical completeness proof* but must not masquerade as a plausible human player.

A game may be formally solvable yet confusing. Measure map backtracking, repeated interaction attempts, idle time before recognizing goals, failure/recovery burden, camera/occlusion problems, unreadable audiovisual cues, checkpoint scarcity and rage-inducing hit sequences. Conversely an expert winning quickly does not prove the tutorial works for a novice. Sampling balance matters: report tester class, episodes, seeds, initial conditions and coverage. Human participants provide subjective evaluation where appropriate; bots cannot manufacture human enjoyment evidence.

## 62.3 Instrumented coverage of game state

Coverage is semantic, not lines of GDScript. Collect visited reachable locations, interacted entities, quest branch transitions, item production/consumption, NPC encounters, combat state, dialogue choices, save migrations, camera regimes and export/install states. Use source/engine semantic IDs so an event in a reference simulator maps to an actual compiled scene/action. Define a critical coverage set of mandatory mechanics and known fragile dependencies. An explorer can find hidden content, but must not invent an action path by accessing internal state not observable to real players.

Track **path coverage**, **transition coverage**, **goal coverage**, **interaction affordance coverage**, **negative state invariant coverage**, and **performance scenario coverage**. Coverage results include actual input tapes and verified game observations, not generator-estimated percentages. Separate "unexplored" from "infeasible"—the latter requires constrained proof or independently checked reason.

## 62.4 The anti-gaming evaluation design

Lock metrics, game versions, tester code, evaluation window and held-out seeds before candidate generation. Avoid optimizing a game and tester on the same exact repeated tape. A candidate that removes gameplay mechanics may score as easy, but should be rejected by required feature-preservation and baseline invariants. A game with a fake internal win flag must be rejected when no observed player goal is completed. A game with constant high frame rate but missing graphics is not a performance success.

Compare with Pareto-aware criteria: mandatory correctness, accessibility, rights and data safety as noncompensable; then quality, diversity, play duration, visual/audio clarity, frame pacing, repair cost and player satisfaction. Record score variance, confidence, failure family and any evaluator disagreement. Protected oracle code and data live outside the generated project and are changed only through normal reviewed source commits.

## 62.5 Causal playtest incident pipeline

On a failure, store an immutable bug dossier with first divergent tick, initial save, source/game package, controller tape, observed frames/audio/logs and expected invariant. Minimize the failing sequence without changing its causal meaning; check reproducibility on a clean target. Route to the correct existing owner: world design, collision/physics, editor, exporter, audio, local AI, install or toolchain. A proposed repair requires a failing parent, passing candidate and independent neighboring regression. A bot cannot suppress the relevant assertion or mark the failure as "unimportant" merely because the patch is hard.

**Exit:** one actual exported original game played by at least two independent tester classes, with recorded win/lose/retry, one counterexample found and repaired or correctly held, replay/save, physical frame observations and source-bound evidence. Record NOT TESTED for any unavailable target device rather than silently using mock playback.

# 63. Offline-first project custody and semantic save migration

**Packet:** FRONTIER-63 | **Leads:** BOT-01 install/backup, BOT-02 data authority, BOT-05 semantic world, BOT-06 game save, BOT-11 UI | **Verifier:** BOT-12. **Existing source anchors:** skeleton/app/private_game_save.py, offline_game_library_audit.py, offline_game_library_relocation.py, offline_mixed_game_library_continuity.py, offline_signed_game_library_audit.py, installed_tree_custody.py and the declared state topology.

The product must remain useful with network disabled, but offline-first does not mean every local file is a primary database. Source projects, user preferences, model assets, gameplay saves, derived indexes, build artifacts and installation state have distinct authorities and upgrade rules. Consolidate real durable state rather than inventing independent project silos for each editor component.

## 63.1 Authority and restoration map

Create a *source-verified* table for every durable domain with canonical writer, logical store, schema version, data classification, retention, snapshot/backup mechanism, restore and concurrent-write policy. Cover authenticated projects, game semantic graph, player saves, asset rights, game library, tool/run receipts, model manifests, local generation cache, crawler evidence, optional vector indexes, installer state and exported packages. A backup is a consistent cross-domain state, not a copy of arbitrary open SQLite/Mongo/Chroma files while writers are active. For each domain, distinguish rebuildable derived state from irreplaceable authored user content.

A full backup must enumerate dependency graph, content digests, project/user ownership and media rights without embedding sensitive secrets in an ordinary export. Private secrets have their own protected recovery route; never scatter keys into game packages. Export may omit private account/device credentials while remaining adequate to restore the user's creative project with independently re-provisioned identity.

## 63.2 Atomic project edit and power-loss semantics

The user changes a game. The app stages semantic patch + affected asset references + expected parent version under current ownership; a successful commit atomically records its authoritative revision and new content references. Rendered previews, vector indexes, thumbnail caches and native builds are projections reconstructed after commit. If the process dies between stages, restart reports the exact prepared/committed/unknown state. It may garbage-collect uncommitted derived media under retention policy but must not assume unreferenced authoritative bytes are safe to delete before reconciliation.

Idempotent replay must never double-grant an inventory item or double-publish a release artifact. A failed commit must not show a saved badge. Two offline devices edited from the same parent require semantic conflict review. Source revision CAS and dependency-aware merge preserve human changes; a text-based blind Git merge is not sufficient for quest/economy semantics.

## 63.3 Game saves and project history must evolve separately

A published game-save schema has immutable game identity, target-compatible schema/version, event cursor, actor/location/inventory/quest/economy/RNG state and integrity. Project edit history may change while a player remains in a legitimate older published game. Migration is explicit: determine compatible versions, stage copy, check invariants, commit atomically and retain last good save until new load proven. Unknown future schemas or corrupted saves must not be overwritten with a new empty game. Offer quarantined export/repair guidance.

Required stateful negative tests: duplicate event replay, missing chunk after cache eviction, concurrent writes, wrong save version, unsupported downgraded engine, stale source asset, partial migration, disk full, interrupted database snapshot and malicious oversized/deserialization input. Check actual game interaction after restoration rather than only JSON shape.

## 63.4 Portable library and source escrow

An offline game library archive contains project manifest, exact content-addressed source and derived assets allowed by rights, schema/toolchain profile, provenance, available native packages, dependency inventory and integrity proofs. Validate entries and safe extraction before importing into the actual existing library owner. Do not allow path traversal, reparse/symlink escape, executable payload abuse or duplicate ownership. On relocation between disks and OSes, normalize paths only through validated mapping and preserve original source identities. If the original native compiler is unavailable, return the editable source and truthful compiler-readiness message.

User-owned game ideas and source should remain exportable in durable documented forms, rather than only through a closed cloud service. A claimed offline mode must actually open an existing project and continue permitted editing while no network is reachable. AI-only features degrade explicitly if model or guard unavailable, never silently transmit private content to a remote substitute.

## 63.5 Disaster and upgrade acceptance

Prove clean restore after service crash, data-volume migration, lost derived Chroma cache, installation upgrade, game package rollback, project relocation and accidental interruption during export. Recreate services from verified base and restored state in a separate environment; compare canonical source/event counts, media digests, active rights, game saves and independently playable target. An archival file that cannot be restored is not backup evidence. Keep app first-install and release holds separate from successful source-only archive checks.

# 64. Bounded autonomous production as a capability and risk compiler

**Packet:** FRONTIER-64 | **Lead:** BOT-04 director | **Partners:** BOT-02 authority, BOT-03 model, BOT-05/06/07/08 content, BOT-09 export, BOT-11 cockpit, BOT-12 QA. **Source anchors:** director_capability_graph.py, jeeves_production_director.py, game_build_queue.py, and existing ToolExecutionReceipt/ResourceBudget/ContextEnvelope contracts.

The production director must compile a human game request into a chain of finite actual operations. Source file count or number of virtual bot roles is not production capacity. A long planning transcript without a playable output is an insufficient result.

## 64.1 Typed campaign request with cost-and-risk envelope

Every admitted campaign has exact user objective, source snapshot, target profile, desired game experience, forbidden changes, acceptable budget/time, mandatory proof obligations and cancellation/approval policy. Decompose into a DAG of source inspection, semantic design, asset authoring, gameplay implementation, validation, engine build, independent play, packaging and optional publication. Each node declares actual canonical owner, read/write scope, needed dependencies, preconditions, postconditions, reversible/irreversible action class, tool authority, resource reservation and expected artifact.

Use source-sha and project-revision identity to guard every mutation. A bot may refine a proposed scene but may not replace a current player's project or widen external crawler egress without another explicit grant. A report of work complete is not an admissible dependency unless accompanied by authoritative tool and artifact receipts.

## 64.2 Scheduling by physical and semantic constraints

Use actual reserved CPU/RAM/GPU/disk/tool slots and declared per-task time budgets. Prefer tasks on the critical path to the first playable loop: authenticated editor; real local model when required; canonical design; player controller; world condition; media bindings; clean target build. A hundred low-priority generated audio variants cannot starve one engine-boot repair. Media and independent levels can parallelize once interfaces are stable; shared schemas, versioned writer authorities and huge mirrored AI trees require serialized ownership or controlled integration.

If a stage hits memory pressure, model outage, invalid rights, failed source conflict or engine import error, stop dependent work or execute a permitted safe alternate. Do not spawn unlimited retry loops to meet a commit/file quota. A partial candidate may remain useful and editable, but should be labelled source-only, not completed game.

## 64.3 Self-directed iteration within deterministic boundaries

The director may choose experiments under finite constraints: adjust level geometry, propose alternate quest prerequisites, regenerate a rights-approved asset, vary camera frame, compare visual style, modify difficulty or narrow a repair. It must not autonomously promote a new model weight, grant publishing rights, override user locks, disable security gates or alter independent test rubrics. A tool proposal is screened by existing authorization and source semantics. All accepted mutations are reviewable; human intervention can revise the objective and cause dependency-aware replan.

Every iteration produces a comparison against a frozen reference with source/game package identity. Store actual failure modes and use them as evidence for next choices. Use uncertainty and value-of-information to stop low-yield experiments. Avoid re-asking a model the identical question with no new evidence and counting its different prose as an improvement.

## 64.4 Meaningful campaign receipts

A final or intermediate campaign record lists actual source revisions committed, playable capabilities observed, exact engine output, QA failures/repaired regressions, resource consumption, unresolved blockers, review approvals and rollback. It distinguishes *planned*, *generated source*, *compiled*, *played*, *packaged* and *released*. If a model fails before any game mutation, the honest result is a recoverable draft and blocker. A verifier signs a separately generated result rather than the director's own success string.

One end-to-end integration sample should prove: user brief → approved two-room game → original art/audio bound → real Godot controls → bug reproduction and repair → save/load → desktop export → author edits and rebuild. Every step binds stable game and source identities. The same campaign, replayed after a forced process kill, must not apply duplicate project edits or duplicate resource charges.
