## 65.1 Proof contract per ticket

Each ticket starts by verifying current source/PR head and mapping to actual existing owner. Builders record the smallest observed missing behavior, then implement in the canonical module and prove it with a test that fails on the old behavior. Tests must be run on finished code, not invented as success statistics. The changed surface includes type/schema compatibility, source/rights, user permission, functional gameplay, crash recovery, target artifact identity and negative cases relevant to the ticket. The independent verifier inspects exact files, input/output digests, environment, test/engine logs and observed video/frame/audio when relevant.

The first integrated golden game remains the shared artifact across specialists. Its world source, project revision, NPCs, assets, quests, input traces and native packages must refer to the same committed project state. A bot may propose a distinct sample to test one genre, but cannot call dozens of isolated demonstrations one complete game. If dependencies are absent, produce a blocked ticket with exact reason; do not fabricate a target or remove a feature to qualify.

## 65.2 New deep proof ladders

**Learning** passes only with approved data partition, actual training/inference effect where claimed, independent held-out evaluation and no policy/weight self-activation. **World streaming** passes only with source/delta reconstruction, actor continuity and physical engine navigation. **Cinematic** passes only with actual target frames/audio and source-to-observation timing. **Multiplayer** passes each profile separately with authoritative state and adversarial input. **Playtest fleet** passes only when independent input-driven targets are used and regressions can genuinely fail. **Offline custody** passes only when real user project/save/media can be restored and played. **Director** passes only when bounded work yields a real project mutation and independently verified playable output.

The user-facing studio report must separate source-present, integrated, engine-tested, device-tested and release-authorized, by feature and target. Draft source PRs, tool-specific mocks or earlier ancestor CI cannot satisfy final-head release proof. A strong new capability must preserve safety, ownership, original-work rights, ability to undo and export, and stable first install.

## 65.3 Practical ordering for the next real implementation cycle

The first integration wave begins with FRT-074, FRT-069, FRT-073 and FRT-076: authority, storage, orchestration and truthful evidence. Next implement a minimal shared first playable with FRT-068, FRT-065 and FRT-079, then FRT-053/054/055/056 for persistent world depth. Media and cinematic FRT-057..060 depend on real engine bindings, not just source cue lists. Learning FRT-049..052 is safely asynchronous and cannot gate all editing by default. Multiplayer FRT-061..064 is optional after single-player integrity and export work. Complete targeted device/export/legal evidence FRT-077/078/080 before any broader marketing or release claim.

A work packet is "done" only when code and real tests satisfy its exact acceptance under an independently reviewed source head. This blueprint itself does not implement, test, merge, train, deploy or release the described capabilities.

# 66. Universal game-mechanics assembly and semantic interoperability across genres

**Build packet:** ULTRA-66 | **Primary:** BOT-05 design/IR and BOT-06 engine | **Consumers:** BOT-07 procedural, BOT-08 media, BOT-09 target compilers, BOT-11 editor, BOT-12 validation. **Observed source anchors:** skeleton/ai/game_builder/advanced_gameplay_runtime.py, advanced_engine_bindings.py, system_editors.py, advanced_quest_director_runtime.py, skeleton/forge/game_mechanics_v2/, skeleton/ai/game_builder/quest_director_solver.py and the already populated genre-specific Godot adapters. This is an integration architecture, not a proposal to erase current game-engine implementations.

The goal is to let the user combine meaningful original game mechanics—movement, quests, NPC behavior, economy, traversal, combat, inventory, dialogue, vehicles, time, puzzles, crafting, base building and procedural worlds—without turning incompatible state models into a tangled accumulation of features. Hundreds of standalone modules only become a game-building platform when they can be composed, edited and exported with stable semantics and measured behavior.

## 66.1 Capability registry with actual implementation states

Build a canonical view of supported gameplay capabilities from existing machine/AI and engine bindings. Each **MechanicCapability** includes semantic ID/version, owner module, valid gameplay domain, input/output state types, deterministic transition rules, emitted gameplay event types, resource/CPU budget, target engine adapters, supported platforms, dependent capabilities, failure conditions, save compatibility, human-editable parameters and minimum proof level. "Module importable" is a different property from "real target playable". A mechanic can be declared **reference-only**, **source-exported**, **engine-executed**, **interactive-tested**, or **target-certified** with evidence, but those labels must be mapped to the canonical state system instead of added as competing enums.

Registration should be strict: no undocumented tools, unknown resource types, duplicate ownership, hidden privileged side effects or type-unsafe transitions. The existing advanced_engine_bindings.py table already connects approved editor identities to simulation start/step/replay for a set of reference runtimes. Extend that mapping with tested target-lowering and runtime readback, not by adding an unbounded reflection loader that imports every Python file or trusts a model-supplied class path. A game with a declared "farming" mechanic must expose actual soil, resources, planting, time and harvesting in the target, rather than a title card labelled farming.

## 66.2 Composition laws and common entities

A composite game is a graph of typed mechanics over one project/world authority. Declare which mechanics share state and how they arbitrate it. For example, crafting consumes inventory components, economy owns prices and transactions, quests observe a committed crafting event, NPC reputation reacts only if witnessed, and animation/audio present results without granting items. A vehicle controller may temporarily own player movement input while player inventory and world location remain one canonical identity. Combat and dialogue must not both claim to advance the same tick independently.

Use a common **semantic action envelope** bound to project revision, actor, input phase, tick, gameplay verb, typed target and validation. Type-check state changes and require deterministic conflict rules: if damage and healing occur in the same tick, specify order; if a door opens and region changes simultaneously, transfer cannot bypass inventory preconditions. A tool should not implement a second private wallet or parallel quest flag map to simplify composition. Each game-owned event must be idempotent where replay or network retransmission can occur.

For a hybrid RPG/farming game, the editor should author an actual farming quest: plant authorized seed, advance a world-time period, water under declared rules, harvest produced crop, trade at market, and trigger an NPC dialogue branch using the same causal event. This one scenario validates at least five interacting mechanic families while preventing fake "gameplay completeness" from isolated JSON operations.

## 66.3 Mechanic adapters as explicit morphisms

An adapter translates one semantic rule into target game-engine operations while preserving declared invariants. Define its domain and codomain and the supported subset: e.g., inventory debit/credit in abstract game state → GDScript resource + committed event; fixed-time quest timer → engine timer tied to authoritative tick; 2D tile navigation → Godot collision, nav and actual player movement. The adapter supplies an explicit mapping from source rule IDs to code/scene node identities, executable inputs, target state readback and failure evidence.

No target is required to support every mechanic. On an unsupported transformation, return a typed build error or request an approved semantic downgrade. Do not silently generate empty scripts for a requested fluid dynamic, climbing mechanic or networking protocol and still label the game complete. The user can choose an alternative target with an honest capability tradeoff. A cross-engine adapter that preserves victory state but loses a mandatory accessibility cue is *not* semantically equivalent for the declared game.

## 66.4 Semantic dependency, revision and selective regeneration

Every mechanic records dependencies on geometry, physics settings, assets, input maps, world events, sound cues and save schema. An AI request to change "make jumping less punishing" should produce a revision of controller jump buffer, fall distance and optionally tutorial affordances; it must invalidate related traversal/physics tests and preserve unrelated story/cosmetic authoring. A new weather event affecting grip must invalidate racing movement tests and road accessibility, not regenerate every dialogue line. A rights or policy change invalidates eligible packages even if the logical gameplay schema is unchanged.

Compile changes incrementally with source-digest pins and dependency closure. A stale agent proposal cannot apply to a newer world; a human-approved manual edit is a lockable constraint, not a fragile chat preference. Expose change-impact explanations in the editor: "This jump-height edit changes six routes, two quest feasibility witnesses and one controller test." Actual counts are computed from current project graph; do not hardcode reassuring numbers.

## 66.5 Emergent gameplay without losing author control

Systems can generate interesting consequences when their interactions are intentionally designed. A drought affects crop yield, which increases market prices, which changes NPC needs and the availability of quest supplies; the player can repair a canal, trade from another region or negotiate with a faction. Each effect is a legal typed event and has balance constraints; stochastic variation uses partitioned RNG and does not invent unlimited resources.

Allow author-defined constraints: must remain completable, no permanent death, at least two nonviolent endings, bounded in-game days, no inaccessible timed inputs, explicit save support. Emergence is tested by generated player action traces and property-based worlds, not by claims of "infinite AI possibility". The designer can freeze specific quests or NPC arcs and vary the ambient systems around them.

## 66.6 Cross-genre acceptance sequence

Test a small library of compositional builds, each sharing the canonical engine/IR owner: platformer + collectible quest; farming + crafting + economy; tactics + dialogue + faction memory; racing + weather + pit/repair; narrative puzzle + multiple endings; survival + procedural chunks + save. For each, run source validation, target build, actual controller path, save/restart, independent logic equivalence and relevant audiovisual/rights checks. Inject three negative mutations: remove one required mechanic adapter, corrupt one shared inventory event, and change one input map after approval. The acceptance suite must fail on the correct dependency.

**Exit:** one original mixed-genre game whose cross-system consequences are observed and independently reproduced on a declared target. A 500-operation editor catalog or a 50-trillion-recipe combinatorial count is not a substitute for that proof.

# 67. Physics, collision, controller fidelity and tactile game-feel laboratory

**Build packet:** ULTRA-67 | **Lead:** BOT-06 | **Peers:** BOT-07 level geometry, BOT-08 animation/audio, BOT-09 targets, BOT-11 input, BOT-12 verification. **Source evidence:** skeleton/ai/game_builder/advanced_physics_runtime.py explicitly describes a bounded fixed-point 2D/3D rigid-body *reference*, not continuous collision or an industrial fluid solver; skeleton/jeeves/game_engine_physics.py models numerical/physics compatibility, while game_engine_input.py normalizes historical digital/analog/touch devices and haptic metadata.

The next layer should make physics and controls work in the exported game with predictable user experience across keyboard/gamepad/touch, not multiply abstract simulation types without engine calibration.

## 67.1 Physical invariants and numerical profiles

For each target mechanic, declare spatial units, handedness, up axis, scale, mass/inertia units, gravity, friction, restitution, damping, fixed timestep, collision layers/masks and numeric precision. Different runtimes may use integer/fixed-point or floating-point arithmetic; cross-runtime equality should compare appropriate conserved and gameplay-relevant invariants rather than demand impossible bitwise equality of floating physics. For a rigid body, position and velocity update must be bounded; contacts must not teleport through static obstacles; energy gain needs an explicit actuator; extreme/NaN inputs are rejected.

Reference state is not the same as Godot physics truth. Build a **PhysicsParityCase** which records reference parameters, target scene/node IDs, injected initial conditions, actions, tick sequence, observed collision manifold or acceptable proxy, final state and tolerances. If native physics differs materially, identify whether adapter units, time step, collision geometry or engine behavior is responsible. Validate high-speed collision with continuous detection or substepping only where target supports it; never claim industrial fluid/cloth accuracy from a tiny fixed-point grid.

## 67.2 Interaction latency and player control

Input semantics include press, hold, release, repeat, analog amplitude, action remap, controller focus and disconnection. A user pressing jump while falling before landing may use a bounded jump buffer; coyote time is an authored grace window, not an engine accident. Movement parameters include acceleration/deceleration, slope tolerance, wall jump, sprint, crouch, climb, camera comfort, knockback and animation-root coupling where relevant. Test all with actual target physics and controlled input tapes.

Use an **input-to-action-to-frame** trace with monotonic clocks and source IDs. Separate input sampling delay, backend transport if a remote preview, physics update, animation selection, rendering and display/audio delivery. For interactive local gameplay, neural generation cannot block critical input handling. Accessibility input assists are explicit player options that retain core progression fairness rather than hidden cheat behavior.

Controller mappings require platform-specific validation. The existing device-normalization reference can serve as a compatibility layer for arcade paddles, digital controls, analog sticks, touch, mouse and optional motion/XR. Do not claim XR device support merely because a schema has a value for it. Every target declares supported physical input classes and missing capabilities honestly.

## 67.3 Collision, navigation and generated-level reachability

Nav graph feasibility must incorporate actual collision shapes, character dimensions, jumps, dynamic obstacles, moving platforms, water/gravity zones, portals and hazardous regions. A path through one tile adjacency is not enough if the character body cannot clear a ledge. Verify spawn is not trapped, goals are physically reachable, mandatory doors have conditions that can be satisfied and the platform has enough timing margin for required movement actions. For physics puzzles, model pushable object mass, constraints, friction and goal completion as legal game actions.

A procedural solver should produce both a logical route and a representative physical replay witness. If an entity would cross an unloaded chunk or miss a collision because of asynchronous streaming, the target cannot be certified by the reference proof. Level edits to terrain height, slope or trigger size invalidate the relevant movement and quest proof. Automated region streaming must not switch collision shape while a player is standing on it without a safe reconciliation rule.

## 67.4 Animation/haptics/audio coupling

Character movement has a single authoritative root displacement policy. Either game physics drives locomotion and animation follows, or accepted animation-root movement feeds target collision correctly. Never add both displacements unintentionally. Footfall events correspond to actual contact transitions, audio samples correspond to surface material, camera shake and haptic output have bounded comfort/accessibility settings. Missing haptic hardware is not a reason to make an interaction undiscoverable. When reduced-motion is enabled, gameplay timing should remain valid while presentation is calmer.

Environmental surfaces—ice, sand, mud, metal, low gravity, current, moving machinery—affect game mechanics through explicit, testable coefficients and authored rule types. Visual shaders may signal slipperiness but cannot secretly change friction. A neural asset proposal never directly mutates physics constants without the existing project approval path.

## 67.5 Physics and game-feel laboratory

Build a standardized suite of rooms: flat movement, slopes, corner collision, jump gaps near reachable threshold, moving platform, knockback, one-way door, water drag, platform through portal, variable frame pacing, disconnected controller and full save/resume. Record known-good controller traces and physical frame observations. Test engine/physics upgrades against this suite and compute regression diffs.

Use at least two device/input classes when support is claimed. Calibrate input latency and tolerances on a fixed hardware profile with actual samples. Inject wrong world scaling, swapped collision mask, missing release action, disabled jump buffer and double root motion; all should fail. A reference-game pass must not certify native game feel. Promote only an observed and editable target behavior with retained failure evidence and rollback.

# 68. Authorized AI coding inside the creator IDE: precise mutation, not model-controlled filesystem

**Build packet:** ULTRA-68 | **Lead:** BOT-04 and BOT-02 | **Consumers:** BOT-05/06 game authors, BOT-09 builds, BOT-11 UI, BOT-12 security/testing. **Source anchors:** skeleton/jeeves/source_edit_gateway.py, source_edit_host.py, repository_file_atlas.py, skeleton/forge/repair.py, frontend/src/features/Jeeves/WorkspaceController.ts and the existing ToolExecutor/source-plane authorities.

The inspected source_edit_gateway.py already requires the ToolExecutor HIGH_IMPACT grant, independent per-call host authorization, a trusted host source editor/lease and a committed-output digest matching the proposed bytes. It accepts narrow deterministic file replacements and an exact indexed source snapshot; a model cannot get write power from the atlas or preview. The new functionality must deepen semantic code editing **within those guarantees**, not bypass them to let an LLM "just run shell".

## 68.1 Context-aware edit intent

A user says "repair the door collision and make the left pathway accessible." The AI first retrieves the exact project graph, relevant source files, engine scripts, test traces, tool capability and source revision. It emits a structured **EditIntent** containing goal, affected entity/rule IDs, source file paths, precondition hashes, proposed semantic diff, expected target behavior, test plan, reversible/irreversible flags, required human permission and finite cost. Retrieval and planning can occur without host write authority. A retrieved README or game asset comment that requests a broader command is inert untrusted data.

The EditIntent is checked against declared file owners, project/tenant, max patches/bytes, tool manifest, safe code language and known generated/manual source boundaries. An agent may not edit release gates, secrets or source-rights records just to satisfy a game task. A model cannot invent nonexistent file contents and submit them as a successful patched result.

## 68.2 Patch production and deterministic host custody

Prefer semantic game-document operations where they exist. For source files without a structured editor, generate minimal exact-context patches with old-content digest, expected replacement and bounded affected range. The trusted host applies them using race-resistant filesystem protections and an exclusive source lease; it verifies after-write bytes and publishes a stable new revision. The file atlas is refreshed incrementally after commit, not treated as a second writer. A patch against changed source fails with a genuine conflict and a replan suggestion.

Generated code can introduce unsafe script execution. Apply parser/syntax validation, domain-specific lint, dependency/ABI checks and sandbox policy before running a target. Game scripts should execute under game target permissions, never with the app backend's privileged environment. Shader/plugin/native code requires a stronger declared permission class and review before compilation. A loose string replacement in a generated script is not permission to run arbitrary imported packages or shell commands.

## 68.3 IDE experience and human control

The UI shows requested outcome, exact file/entity diff, before/after gameplay effect, validation plan, cost estimate, rights/security implications and rollback path. The user can approve selected safe edits, reject a subset, refine their intent or lock authored code from regeneration. For unreviewed large changes, group diff by semantic effect rather than dumping hundreds of files with no narrative. A "repair" button must actually dispatch a granted tool call or clearly be suggestion-only.

Jeeves should support multi-step projects with precise checkpoints: inspect, propose, approve, mutate, compile, test, show evidence. A model may suggest a code generation campaign but must not treat its own response as proof that the host wrote bytes. An error message from a real compiler should remain visible even if the model proposes a follow-up. The user owns the game and can edit it without AI.

## 68.4 Executable repair and regression protocol

After a candidate patch, run the parser/type tests for the modified source, the relevant engine import/launch, an actual input trace and the independent regression set. If the fix is a shared emitter/compiler bug, add a source-level regression proving future games get the repair rather than only patching one exported artifact. For a project-only authored rule, preserve engine owner and semantic history. A repair may not delete the scenario, disable the oracle, or turn a real collision into a purely cosmetic door-open animation.

Bound attempts; preserve last-good source. If tests fail, attach exact compiler/engine logs and minimal counterexample. Conflicting changes by another bot/human require source-version fencing. If the host cannot prove safe file custody on the current platform, return BLOCKED rather than doing an unsafe ad-hoc write.

## 68.5 Security and adversarial acceptance

Attack with malicious repository comments, fake tool messages, a stale atlas hash, a symlink-target swap, concurrent modification, source file larger than limits, wrong user project, missing HIGH_IMPACT grant, forged approval receipt and code attempting to read secrets. No privileged write may occur. Then perform one legitimate authorized edit of a real generated Godot project and prove it changes gameplay on the exported target. The result records host source revision and new digest, human approval, test artifacts and all remaining release holds.

# 69. Accessibility and localization as first-class game compilation constraints

**Build packet:** ULTRA-69 | **Lead:** BOT-11 and BOT-08 | **Peers:** BOT-05 narrative, BOT-06 controls, BOT-09 exports, BOT-12 accessible verification. **Observed anchors:** skeleton/ai/game_builder/advanced_accessibility_runtime.py, advanced_localization_runtime.py, frontend/src/features/Jeeves/GamePlayViewport.tsx, menu_accessibility.py and the typed game/editor client contracts.

The reference accessibility runtime actually simulates remapped action dispatch, alternative cues, subtitle text and reduced motion preferences, while explicitly disclaiming real screen-reader hardware/compliance audits. The localization reference actually resolves four declared locales (English, French, Arabic, Japanese), including plurals and RTL/fallback logic, but does not claim unlimited languages or certified translations. These are good bounded starting points. The completion path is **exported-game accessible play and correctly localized interaction**, not a bigger static locale list.

## 69.1 Accessibility requirements flow into design IR

An admitted game brief declares essential actions, expected input devices, readability, sensory alternatives, cognitive-load concerns, timing demands and minimum accessibility target. Each required game action must have at least one reachable input binding under the selected profile; each mandatory cue must have a usable nonexclusive sensory representation; each goal path must be completable using declared accessible controls. These are compilable constraints with proof requirements, not just a collection of settings checkboxes.

Represent adjustable options: remap inputs, hold/toggle behavior, font scaling, contrast palettes, captions/subtitles, reduced motion, flashing intensity limits, camera shake, difficulty/assist options, time extensions and pause state. Default values and constraints must survive project build, save/restart and target export. Do not invent a global WCAG certification for every 3D game; scope checks to applicable application UI standards and actual gameplay accessibility evidence.

## 69.2 Input remapping with conflict resolution

A remap is a transaction over an input action graph. Rebinding jump to confirm must not silently remove the only available confirm or back command. Detect duplicate bindings, inaccessible menu navigation, controller disconnect, focus traps and platform-reserved keys. Provide a reset/recovery route operable with accessible controls. Runtime input maps and editor preview must consume the same mapping revision, and the actual exported target must demonstrate remap behavior. A successful reference ACTIONS simulation does not prove a real controller works.

Assist profiles can enlarge timing windows, simplify simultaneous inputs or offer alternative puzzle interactions when the game's design permits. An action under an assist should still pass through canonical gameplay state, and the game must explicitly label modified scoring/competition behavior where relevant. No accessibility setting should transmit private health information or silently infer a sensitive trait.

## 69.3 Source-owned localization catalog

All player-facing text in quests, dialogue, menus, subtitles, tutorials, achievements and errors has stable string ID, source locale, version, placeholders, plural/gender/select grammar where supported, size/layout budget and context note. A translation candidate retains rights and reviewer origin. Automatically generated translations are not certified until reviewed and tested in their actual UI/scene. Never assume words have the same length or grammar across languages. Typed placeholders cannot become injected scripts or unsafe markup.

For Arabic, demonstrate actual RTL direction, bidi handling, mirrored controls only when semantically appropriate, correct joining and numeric display; for Japanese, verify line breaking and glyph coverage; for French, plural/length. Locale fallback is deterministic and visible when unreviewed or missing. A target without a suitable font must fail its locale qualification or package an appropriately licensed glyph set. Broken localization must not corrupt quest IDs or gameplay logic.

## 69.4 Multimodal accessible gameplay cues

Sound effects must have captions or visual/tactile alternatives when they convey mandatory information; color-coded puzzles need symbols, shapes, patterns or text beyond hue; cinematic dialogue needs subtitles and timing with actual sound; reduced-motion modes avoid excessive camera shake and flashing without invalidating movement or collision. Target engine captures and accessible UI trees are the evidence, not a declarative "supports accessibility" field.

Screen-reader and keyboard-only creator journeys need end-to-end testing: first setup, create project, edit world, approve AI change, play accessible preview, inspect errors, export. Native game UI may have different assistive technology support from the web studio; qualify each separately and retain honest limitations.

## 69.5 Accessibility/localization regression suite

Test a generated puzzle across all currently declared supported locales, with long dialogue, Arabic RTL text, Japanese glyphs, plural forms, dynamic type scaling and fallback. Play the game with remapped controls and no mouse. Disable sound and validate critical cues; enable reduced motion and validate camera/mission progression. Inject missing font, unbound confirm action, color-only essential clue, late voice subtitle and a translated placeholder mismatch; all must fail appropriate gating. Produce an independent report with actual engine views, input sequences and accessible interaction—not just pure translation lookup outputs.

**Exit:** one complete game can be edited and played to a real ending using one alternate accessible control scheme and localized target UI with observed correct gameplay state, source rights and saved settings.

# 70. Real GPU rendering and proof-carrying frame graphs

**Packet:** NEXT-70 | **Lead:** BOT-08 | **Partners:** BOT-05 world, BOT-06 gameplay, BOT-09 export, BOT-11 editor, BOT-12 independent verification. **Inspected source:** skeleton/game/render/flgb_render_runtime.py owns immutable RenderPass/RenderGraph, MaterialNode/MaterialGraph, ShaderCompileRequest/Receipt, TextureRequest, MeshArtifact, Light, ShadowRequest, CameraRig, RenderCheckpoint and RenderRecoveryDecision. The render_graph.py and render_recovery.py files re-export these types. This packet is integration on these actual owners, not another GPU execution authority.

A graph of passes, materials and light requests is a useful structural description; it is not evidence that a real target generated pixels. The next engineering frontier is taking one committed project revision and camera, importing/binding the corresponding geometry/materials, running an admitted actual engine or GPU backend, observing its output frames and comparing those to gameplay events. Renderer completion requires both a correct graph and an observed, playable scene.

## 70.1 Cross-pass hazards, memory lifetimes and backend admission

RenderGraph currently topologically orders declared dependencies and rejects cycles. RenderPass disallows reading and writing a logical resource within the same pass. Extend the validated projection to include *cross-pass* hazards: read before a valid producer, two overlapping writes, lost synchronization, incompatible resource format, invalid depth/stencil access, unsupported compute stage, stale shader reflection and aliased memory still in use. A directed acyclic graph alone cannot establish these GPU safety properties.

Model resource lifetime and usage through existing render authority. Each transient image/buffer identifies its producer, consumers, format, dimensions, physical allocation compatibility, GPU access stage and release fence. An allocator may alias memory only after it can show that all prior reads/writes have completed. Do not let a model reorder graphics passes to claim speed without proving matching final frames. Target-specific import/barriers are typed operations, not arbitrary user-selected shader callbacks that execute in the privileged backend.

Admit real target capability first: engine/version, graphics API, texture formats, shader stages, memory and draw budgets, frame capture support and dependency versions. If a requested compute or mesh shader is unsupported, return a truthful unsupported feature with optional reviewed fallback, rather than an empty render pass. Keep source-only graph checks separate from real target execution.

## 70.2 Shader and material semantics

The existing ShaderCompileRequest contains source digest, stage, target and defines; ShaderCompileReceipt binds compiler/binary/reflection/warning digests. Require the actual compiler process and imported shader bytes before making a runtime claim. Validate stage interfaces, vertex layout, descriptor/binding types, uniform alignment, texture colorspaces, sampler limits, shader feature flags, deterministic build identity and runtime compile errors. A digest over invented compiler output is invalid evidence.

Materials need explicit physically based conventions: linear-versus-sRGB channels; roughness/metallic/normal/occlusion semantics; opacity ordering; tangent normal conventions; alpha premultiplication; emission and shadow participation. Editor-visible material parameters must map to real engine shader uniforms or declare unsupported. Original authored textures retain provenance, rights and reversible transforms. A complex neural-looking surface preview is not a native material until a real target renders it from licensed bytes.

Advanced candidates—clustered lights, virtualized mesh/texture streaming, GPU-driven culling, temporal upscaling, volumetric fog, global illumination and neural denoising—are *optional experiments*. Each must beat a pinned baseline in actual frame quality and frame-time budget without weakening device, safety or user-perception requirements.

## 70.3 Geometry, collision and visual affordances

MeshArtifact declares topology, vertex/index counts and bounds digest, but this does not prove that a GPU buffer or skinned scene exists. For any produced prop/character, bind source mesh bytes, target import ID, material, transform, camera visibility, collision source and player interaction. Test winding, UVs/tangents, normals, scale/up-axis, degenerate triangles, shader availability and target draw limits. Link visible and physical identities so a bridge shown to the player is traversable according to its actual collider.

CameraRig source coordinates/FOV must lower to a real target camera. Verify frame composition, aspect ratios, depth/clipping, character visibility, required quest clues, subtitle safe zones and reduced-motion constraints. A formally valid camera looking at a wall is not a gameplay-qualified view. Source-to-render-to-collision association is mandatory for interactive scenes; losing any link invalidates target proof.

## 70.4 Texture streaming, lights and device pressure

The existing plan_texture_streaming and plan_shadows choose admissible requests under byte/texel caps. Extend decisions into *observed physical resource residency* through current capacity managers, never a second GPU ledger. Use camera proximity, velocity, scene semantics, required quest cues, active UI, true VRAM consumption, upload fences, shader warmup and thermal/swap pressure. Evict cosmetic mip levels before mission-critical sprites or HUD. Do not reclaim capacity until the worker/driver confirms release.

Use bounded fallbacks: lower texture mips, simpler shadows, reduced particles, cheaper material, controlled draw distances. Never hide a mandatory collectible merely to meet FPS, or advertise active collision before geometry is ready. Track p95/p99 frame time, shader stalls, resource peaks and screenshot-level visual defects. Different target hardware tiers receive different admitted caps and evidence.

## 70.5 Renderer recovery and proof

On device loss, discard invalid GPU handles, rebuild derived resources from approved source, rebind the last committed project scene/camera and preserve game event/save history. Render recovery cannot mint inventory or overwrite a human project. Unsupported/failed shaders must not enter endless reload loops. Capture actual engine frames on a declared supported target while player input moves through a scene with lighting, one rigged actor, texture LOD, a quest item, UI and collision. Induce missing shader, malformed mesh, GPU pressure and context loss. Verify real visible fallbacks or precise holds, not a metadata-only "rendered" flag. Retain graph/source/asset/target/frame identities in every acceptance receipt.

# 71. Full original media foundry with target-native asset custody

**Packet:** NEXT-71 | **Lead:** BOT-08 | **Partners:** BOT-02 rights, BOT-03 approved generation, BOT-05 design, BOT-06 engine, BOT-09 packaging, BOT-12 QA. **Inspected source:** skeleton/ai/game_builder/studio_asset_pipeline.py creates original pixel tile bytes, PNG previews and portable media; studio_sprite_authoring.py accepts exact six semantic 8×8 indexed sprites or its specifically bounded artist PNG. Selected GB/CGB/NES/SMS/Game Gear emitters consume generated tiles, while other listed targets may support previews only. Do not confuse a portable preview with a native embedded game asset.

## 71.1 Source asset ledger and transform graph

An asset has canonical content digest, tenant/project owner, origin, author/consent/rights, medium and format, exact dimensions/bounds, semantic role, transformations, version/seed/model settings if generated, allowed targets, source references, revocation state and dependent outputs. Its bytes are admitted through existing artifact custody, not by an arbitrary model-named path. Each transform—decode, crop, quantize, atlas, rig, bake, resample, compress, import, export—is reproducible or explicitly records nondeterministic physical output and its digest.

A text description of artwork cannot be counted as pixels. A PNG preview does not prove a cartridge program consumes the tile bytes. A sprite atlas is not an animated engine character until actual input drives frame/state changes. Rights clearance to study an image or video is not permission to redistribute it or train on it. Source withdrawal invalidates dependent media/export lineage without deleting independent user-owned work.

## 71.2 2D sprite, palette and font production

Support actual sprite drawing/import, layers, alpha, pivots, collision/hit boxes, animation frames, tilemaps, texture atlases, palette controls, UI states and accessible variants. Every import validates decompressed size, dimensions, colorspace and pixel data under bounded decoder resources. Tile codecs must round-trip tested input to output bytes; renderer check compares actual target import and UV/sample alignment. Quantization/dithering records palette and algorithm, and does not silently discard artist-approved detail.

Cartridge targets have real palette/bank/VRAM/tile memory constraints. The current six-tile structure must not silently accept a larger atlas by truncation. More tiles require actual banked scene handling and relevant source/game assembly changes, then emulator and where possible hardware proof. Modern game projects can offer richer animation and resolution while retaining source pixel identity, consistent character silhouette and registered target features.

Text is an asset too: font rights, glyph range, locale shaping, scaling, contrast and subtitle layout should be tested in the actual game, not merely in a source catalog. An unsupported script such as Arabic RTL without correct shaping or Japanese glyph fallback must be reported honestly.

## 71.3 3D model, rig and material pathway

Admit authorized procedural geometry, user-authored mesh, modular building blocks or model-generated candidates. Validate scale/up-axis, mesh topology, UV, tangent/normal, bounds, material channels, skin weights and skeleton parent graph before engine import. Derived LOD, normal maps, baked textures or mesh simplifications retain original source rights and reversible editing metadata. Physically visible behavior and collider navigation are separate acceptance dimensions.

For character production, retain a stable identity/canon definition and actual animation tree mapping. An idle/walk/run/attack proposal passes only when the target renderer displays the motion and gameplay root/collision state agrees. Optional neural reconstruction, Gaussian visual fields or generative retopology are research features until editable engine-supported output is actually proven. A gorgeous render cannot substitute for a controllable original character.

## 71.4 Audio, voice, VFX and cross-media sync

Audio cues need real decodable samples or authorized synthesis, mixer bus, timing, loudness, spatial attributes, captions and rights. The logical audio scheduler cannot itself attest physical playback. VFX need actual engine emitter, GPU/CPU particle budget, responsive gameplay cue and accessible alternative. Cinematics bind source dialogue, shot, actor expression/pose, audio sample and subtitle cue on a versioned timeline. Skipping, pausing, localizing or restoring the scene cannot double-commit rewards.

AI media must be permissioned and bounded by user privacy and commercial rights. Real-person voice/likeness sources require appropriate consent; do not train on private media by default. Content from a crawler remains research evidence until approved for use and transformation. Any unavailable provider leaves the user with a clear manual/procedural asset path, not a fabricated generated file.

## 71.5 Usage-based asset acceptance

An asset is **produced**, **decoded**, **engine-imported**, **bound to scene/gameplay**, **observed in real play**, **retained through rebuild/save**, and **eligible for release** as separate milestones. The user cockpit should show actual usage and orphan dependencies. A large unused library can be valuable but cannot be counted as a more complete playable game. Test missing clip/texture, PNG bomb, incorrect tile count, invalid rig, revoked rights and stale shader asset. One original small game should visibly and audibly consume the same accepted assets in a clean-target executable, with exact digests and independent evidence.

# 72. Creator workbench: unified game digital twin and source-to-play debugging

**Packet:** NEXT-72 | **Lead:** BOT-11 | **Partners:** BOT-02 identity, BOT-04 Jeeves, BOT-05 world, BOT-06 input, BOT-08 media, BOT-09 build, BOT-12 usability. **Observed surfaces:** GameSceneTimeline.tsx provides an editable SVG-based timeline; GameBuildWorkflowPanel.tsx manages build plans, previews, auth scope and cancellable requests; GamePlayViewport.tsx connects to game play; Forge panels expose detailed source authoring. The goal is not more separate panels but one coherent, inspectable product.

## 72.1 One canonical project, many synchronized views

Show world scene/hierarchy, mechanics/events, assets, character rigs, production timeline, actual play, builds, QA/evidence and Jeeves suggestions as views of one project revision. A selection of one door links source entity, quest predicate, collider, mesh, trigger event, animation and native playtest. If any link is missing, display the integration gap rather than invent it. UI state such as zoom or drag is ephemeral; project revisions and tool receipts belong to the existing authoritative backend/engine.

A human project edit is source-CAS guarded. Another collaborator or AI working from an old revision must see a conflict and replan instead of overwriting the user's latest change. A browser offline draft is clearly not a committed project. Switching auth account/project fences old requests and private cached views.

## 72.2 Spatial and timeline editing

Spatial tools need scene hierarchy, layers, camera, tile/terrain brush, prefab/actor placement, collision and nav affordances, event triggers, lighting/material controls and asset previews where target-supported. Unavailable features should be explicit. Large worlds require virtualized trees and lazy thumbnails; never load all future chapters or all hypothetical chunks into the device. Use source IDs for selections, not names guessed by an LLM.

Timeline editing binds keyframe, actor, camera, audio, caption, interpolation, logical time and optional gameplay consequence. Scrubbing presentation must not mutate authoritative quest/inventory. A moved dialog cue updates dependent subtitle and camera timing with clear changed-node diff. A target that cannot lower the requested animation returns an actionable build error rather than an empty clip.

## 72.3 Actual playable comparison and repair

Provide design preview beside last verified engine capture when useful. Label source-only, reference simulator, headless replay, live interactive engine and physical target proof separately. A tool-generated image in the viewport cannot be labelled a current playable native screenshot. An input recording maps player action → game tick → world event → scene transform → frame/audio output. A bug report can jump to the first divergence, its source rule and a minimal reproducer.

Jeeves can propose a patch with exact file/semantic IDs, parent revision, expected effects, budget and testing. The user can approve or reject. Tool execution needs the real current permissions; a chat statement never becomes a host source write or release grant. Preserve manual art/canon locks across regeneration.

## 72.4 User-journey and accessibility acceptance

A novice should be able to create a small original world, place player and door, request a quest, edit a rule, observe a real engine play, save/restart, compare result, approve one AI repair and export a source/target with truthful proof labels. An expert should inspect typed graphs, build dependencies, raw source, rights, test logs and performance. Run keyboard-only, gamepad/touch where claimed, reduced-motion, large text and screen-reader journeys. Buttons must be real operations or unambiguously read-only; a progress spinner alone is not evidence of a running worker.

# 73. Exact-package release assurance and trustworthy consumer delivery

**Packet:** NEXT-73 | **Lead:** BOT-09 | **Independent owners:** BOT-02 rights/security and BOT-12 QA. **Observed source:** consumer_release_assurance.py validates role-separated HMAC evidence kinds RIGHTS, PLAYTEST, HARDWARE, ACCESSIBILITY, LOCALIZATION, MALWARE, CODESIGN, PLATFORM_PERMISSION and PUBLICATION against one exact source manifest. It explicitly notes HMAC proves configured-key custody, not legal correctness. native_release_intake.py byte-verifies bounded local artifacts through no-follow descriptor-anchored paths, while deliberately refusing to claim compiler execution, native play, legal review or release. studio_godot_qualification.py performs headless GDScript replay parity and expressly does not claim visible framebuffer, native binary export, hardware controller or release approval.

## 73.1 Evidence DAG and scope

A candidate package binds project/source revision, build/toolchain digests, executable bytes, bundled asset/rights inventory, target OS/architecture, save schema, supported input, localization/accessibility, independent QA, malware/security scan, signing and human distribution decision. Each evidence node has issuer role, exact subject, produced timestamp, dependency identities, tool/runner, policy version and freshness. A proof for an old package cannot qualify a new binary merely because both came from the same project name.

Classify separately: source valid; bytes exact; compiler actually executed; game behavior observed; clean target device compatible; security/rights approved; publication authorized. If the binary changes, dependent malware and gameplay proof must be rechecked. If rights change, the affected export eligibility is re-evaluated even if bytes remain unchanged. Preserve independent evidence that is still current.

## 73.2 Build and game acceptance cannot be inferred

A successful source-to-C11 or GDScript emitter is a source artifact, not a Windows executable. A file starting with MZ or ELF is not proof of successful toolchain or runtime execution. A headless engine script replay proving end state does not demonstrate pixels, audio, real player input or clean device install. The user-facing release view must show these as separate explicit states.

For each claimed target, require real toolchain invocation, isolated build, binary/asset import, clean-host launch, controller-to-game goal completion, save/restart and relevant physical audio/graphics tests. Unsupported targets remain source-only or unavailable. A platform SDK absent from the host is not a reason to fabricate executable bytes.

## 73.3 Security, rights and signoff

Keep code-signing keys and trusted HMAC keys out of game manifests. Independently signed role evidence cannot be self-issued by the model or inferred from a favourable QA summary. A rights review verifies original and imported material under the actual intended use; passing a structural credits check is insufficient for legal clearance. Malware/active-content scanning applies to the final package, and scanner unavailable is not scanner clean. Public storefront or paid distribution additionally needs entitlement/payment and platform approval, separately from offline self-export.

An AI worker may prepare a candidate but cannot unilaterally publish it. Exact-head CI, architecture/source parity, security checks, physical target and human approvals remain independent noncompensable gates. A draft PR is not release authority.

## 73.4 Recovery, rollback and negative tests

Retain a last-known-good package, versioned save compatibility and a rollback plan. A failed update cannot erase player progress, and a rights withdrawal must block ineligible redistribution without deleting unrelated authored source. Inject one changed binary byte, reviewer-role substitution, stale evidence, forged HMAC, missing license notice, no compiler binary, failed controller replay, unsafe path/symlink and unavailable malware scanner. Verify each rejects at the appropriate stage while accurately retaining unrelated valid proof. Publication is allowed only after every required exact-subject gate and an authorized final decision.

# 74. Experimental game optimization without score gaming: multifactor causal improvement

**Engineering packet:** NEXT-74 | **Primary:** BOT-12 scientific QA and BOT-06 gameplay | **Partners:** BOT-03 model learning, BOT-04 campaign execution, BOT-05 world/quests, BOT-08 visual/audio, BOT-11 UI. **Inspected sources:** skeleton/jeeves/game_studio_multifactor.py uses a typed set of legal registered settings, bounded pair/three-way covering, source-replayed ablations, held-out seed separation and optional Q-policy learning; it explicitly does not improve global Jeeves weights. skeleton/jeeves/game_studio_scenario_lab.py executes bounded independent reference environments and is explicit that sales rankings are neither game-mechanic proof nor rights to copy third-party content. skeleton/ai/game_builder/quality_debt.py defines a bounded ratcheting debt ledger across protected axes.

The next product frontier is **genuinely better player experiences generated from evidence**, not a model that makes claims of superiority after producing more words or altering test scores. The system needs a controlled experimental design that can identify causal improvements and reject unsafe regressions. An experiment can be narrow and still valuable if it changes a user-facing behavior on a real target.

## 74.1 Pre-registered factors and observable outcomes

Every optimization campaign defines a source project revision, target engine/binary, real admitted hardware profile, fixed initial saves/seeds, game mechanic, evaluation budget and independent judge. The factor graph contains actual editable settings such as movement acceleration, jump buffer, quest prerequisites, enemy telegraph, loot distribution, encounter rate, camera motion, UI scale, lighting cues, music mixer and generated-world density. A requested but unimplemented factor is **unsupported**, not a pretend synthetic output. The current multifactor tool already supports bounded registered source knobs; expand only through real owner-backed capabilities.

A factor trial records exact baseline values, candidate values, transformation receipt, affected source IDs, expected physical effect, evaluation conditions and outcome. Control confounding: run one-factor ablations where possible; cover selected pairwise interactions when changes couple (e.g., jump height × platform distance, enemy speed × attack warning, lighting × clue contrast). Three-way designs may be necessary for complex affordances but consume more budget; use legal bounded designs rather than factorial explosion. Hold out seeds and project families against adaptive selection.

## 74.2 Quality score is a vector with hard constraints

Candidate metrics include completion, softlock rate, player command success, confusion/backtracking, fair difficulty, narrative branch significance, visible/audible feedback, accessibility, renderer frame pacing, memory, export size, build duration, model inference latency and user review. Not all dimensions can be collapsed to one number. Rights, privacy, authorization, unrecoverable save loss, inability to finish a mandatory goal and broken target support are **noncompensable gates**. A candidate with faster FPS but an invisible required clue must fail even if an aggregate aesthetic score rises.

Separate objective verifiers from subjective review. The player may prefer deliberately difficult games; a designer's intended theme can override a general-purpose "fun" predictor. A model can suggest hypotheses, but the independent tester checks real game behavior. Human playtest participants can report preference with uncertainty and anonymized/consented observations; don't fabricate human judgements from synthetic personas.

## 74.3 Causal inference, variance and repeatability

Run matched baseline and candidate on identical package class, hardware, seeds, tester skill profile and initial state. Randomize order when thermal or hardware carryover could affect results, and report within-arm variance. Use predeclared confidence/abstention policy rather than cherry-picking one impressive run. If a variant differs simultaneously in game engine, shader, quest goals and test controller, the experiment is confounded: classify exploratory, not causal superiority. In counterfactual experiments, changing one input step can reveal response differences, but is not proof of general mechanic mastery.

Negative benchmarks intentionally expose score gaming: removing enemies, hiding a hard quest, changing terminal predicates, shortening play length without preserving experience, weakening accessibility standards or disabling collision tests. The quality-debt ratchet prevents gradual accumulation of small compromises whose total impact would silently degrade the product. Protected-axis debt remains a release hold, not a score weight to trade against speed.

## 74.4 Active experiment selection and stopping

Choose the next trial by estimated value of information, uncertainty reduction, cost and potential user benefit, bounded by real ResourceBudget. Do not spawn unlimited self-play or repeated model turns when the testing setup has not changed. Stop when improvements plateau, required tests regress, critical pressure is observed, comparison is underpowered, source changes invalidate baseline or user approval expires. Preserve last-good version and exact rejected candidates for future diagnosis.

An optimization can be promoted only on an authorized project revision with current dependent proofs. The model should explain causal uncertainty rather than assert certainty from sparse results. Release certification remains a separate independent procedure. The experiment system may recommend a candidate that the artist intentionally rejects; respecting creator agency is not a failed metric.

## 74.5 Acceptance

Run a bounded original platformer and puzzle comparison using factors that actually exist in target code. Show held-out baseline/candidate input traces, game state, frame timing and at least one meaningful improvement under frozen requirements. Corrupt a mandatory path, remove a visual hint and change a saved-game format in candidate trials; the gate must reject these despite any faster execution. Repeat with a fixed source seed and demonstrate actual variance/limits. Model training or toolchain hardware tests are not inferred from reference lab results.

# 75. Jeeves creative campaigns: exactly bounded physical execution and source-level custody

**Engineering packet:** NEXT-75 | **Primary:** BOT-04 | **Partners:** BOT-02 policy/owner, BOT-03 local provider, BOT-05/06 game engines, BOT-08 media, BOT-09 build, BOT-11 UI, BOT-12 independent review. **Inspected sources:** skeleton/ai/game_builder/studio_execution_plane.py contains explicit EXECUTABLE_TOOLS, a bounded MAX_EXECUTION_STEPS=32, typed ExecutedToolReceipts and fail-closed external/research IDs, while studio_campaign_assurance.py is a read-side assurance projection and separately admits operator-only native ROM compilation. These safeguards need to remain stronger than a model's wish to perform an action.

## 75.1 Creator request as a capability-constrained campaign

Compile a game request into a finite work DAG whose nodes specify canonical owner, exact source revision, goal/expected game effect, tool identifier, permitted arguments, read/write footprint, financial/CPU/GPU/disk token budget, external dependencies, policy snapshot and verifiable postconditions. A work node may request another review but cannot spawn an unbounded recursive hierarchy of agents or create its own production permissions. The existing authorized tool fabric decides actual availability; a tool advertised in a model context is not necessarily executable.

The first vertical slice should be authored and verified as one complete game across agents. BOT-05 owns semantic world/quest changes; BOT-06 gameplay/input; BOT-08 media; BOT-09 actual target packaging. The director coordinates receipts and user approvals, not write access over all those owners. The user's intent remains pinned and inspectable; design suggestions are candidate alternatives, not permission to remove required difficulty or content to fit a limited budget.

## 75.2 Workload-aware admission and safe fallbacks

Interactive game rendering/editor actions have protected capacity. Background model reasoning, asset synthesis, crawler research, large compiler runs and experiments consume finite admitted slots. A logical virtual worker is an orchestration lane, not physical inference throughput. When memory/disk/thermal limits are approached, pause or safely cancel lower-priority work, checkpoint where supported and leave committed game state intact. Worker death must be physically reconciled before GPU/CPU reservations are released.

If a valid actual local model is not ready, the user can continue deterministic authoring and source-only export where supported. Jeeves should report model-unavailable rather than simulate tool-calling success or secretly send private prompts to a hosted provider. If a legal native toolchain is absent, preserve source and request a real operator step. If research access is denied, use approved local knowledge or ask for an authorized source; denial does not imply product failure outside that optional scope.

## 75.3 Human steerability and stable revision patches

At checkpoints, a human may inspect plan, generated world graph, art direction, playable preview, source diff and budget. They can reject a variant, lock a character outfit, modify a quest predicate or request a different target. A change becomes an authorized new revision; pending jobs whose preconditions depend on the old source are invalidated or re-planned. Two agents cannot silently overwrite the same project file via separate cached source snapshots. Source-edit gateway policy and high-impact grants remain active even when work originates from a friendly UI button.

Every patch has a compensation or rollback plan. An irreversible external publication/payment operation requires stronger user authority. A model-generated "approval obtained" string is not a valid signed decision. A report of "game packaged" requires exact artifact bytes and verifiable build trace; source-only build logs should not be substituted.

## 75.4 Crash-safe receipts, job status and stage completion

Each tool execution result has exact input/output digests, source/tool identity, predecessor receipt, evidence, status and idempotency. If a tool call times out after a possible external side effect, the state is unknown until the canonical owner reports an outcome. Blind reissue can duplicate game assets, charges or edits. Cancellation signals must propagate to actual running subprocesses and model slots. A successful stage is one whose observed postcondition holds, not one whose model reply ends in "done".

The campaign dashboard should show four dimensions: accepted project changes, target proof level, current physical worker load, and unresolved blockers. It should not claim 100% because every node in a planning DAG has been assigned. The existing studio_execution_history.py is a bounded append-only, source-bound history of qualification reports; it is not an autonomous monitoring engine or store of raw game/model content. Keep operational logs and artifact custody in their proper declared domains.

## 75.5 Multi-bot integration rejection cases

Reject a tool handoff that broadens read roots, expired human approval, stale source parent, duplicate idempotency with changed payload, unavailable native compiler, crawler text that requests privileged code, release worker acting as legal issuer and a cancelled model whose physical process remains alive. Positive campaign: create original two-room game, human edit a quest, generate bound media, play through a native engine, repair a tested bug, save/restart, build clean target and show exact source/evidence. Retain all existing first-install/release holds not proven by that target.

# 76. Qualification conveyor, failure taxonomy and proof freshness under massive repository churn

**Engineering packet:** NEXT-76 | **Primary:** BOT-12 and BOT-02 | **Partners:** all lanes. **Inspected sources:** studio_campaign_assurance.py declares separate source, pixel parity, browser playthrough, Godot headless, canvas capture, emulator, controller, audio, rights, recovery and signoff gates; studio_execution_history.py stores bounded hash-linked E2E run summaries; studio_history_backup.py backs up *only* validated history segments and explicitly does not capture games/media/weights; studio_compiled_psg_parity.py checks real linked ROM music tables but not physical audible hardware output.

## 76.1 Evidence graph over the exact candidate head

Every qualification claim binds source SHA, changed paths, project revision, engine/game package, toolchain, test fixture, reviewer and policy. A source-only success cannot be promoted to live play by writing a newer assurance report. A binary-header or linker symbol match is useful narrow evidence; it does not assert emulator, controller, audio DAC or physical platform behavior. Positive evidence is retained at its real level; superseded or changed dependencies invalidate only the affected downstream proofs.

The CI conveyor must understand architecture/AI mirror parity, dependency quality, security/malware, frontend/backend functionality, genuine game runtime, native install, hardware and release rights as independent gates. One green Secret Scanning result does not erase a failed source graph, and a real Godot headless replay does not certify a customer Windows laptop. Queued, skipped, cancelled, pending, mock-only and ancestor checks must remain separately classified.

## 76.2 Causal blocker taxonomy and minimum repairs

Classify first reproducible blocker by domain: source/AI-tree mismatch; tool schema; parent PR; game IR semantics; model/reviewer/epoch; installation Mongo/Chroma/secrets; target compiler absent; Godot scene/script; bad import; user input; GPU/media; source rights; security; stale CI; hardware device; or release signoff. Identify the first causally upstream failed condition and the exact paths/artifacts. Avoid rerunning every expensive workflow before resolving an obvious deterministic source mismatch; after a real repair, rerun appropriate checks on the exact new head.

Each failure has a red/green reproducer, minimal proposed change, negative regression, affected dependency set, owner, rollback and release-hold impact. An integration change that alters tool boundaries requires architecture/permission review even if game unit tests pass. If a failure cannot be reproduced because hardware or credentials are missing, record BLOCKED/UNVERIFIED rather than a speculative pass.

## 76.3 Immutable history, archives and truth continuity

The execution history is a record of observed assurance reports, not source gameplay footage. A history backup cannot replace a full project backup; separate authoritative source/artifact/save custody persists through upgrades. A hash-linked report chain provides tamper evidence but not real-world truth of an underlying tester's observation. Independent verifier must confirm underlying evidence and issuer role.

Prevent history truncation, duplicate event inflation, ancestor-success reuse and stale stream-terminal summaries. Use finite segment limits and sealed archive transitions. If a run was superseded, retain its historical result but exclude it from the current readiness decision. If current HEAD changes the target game package, expired game playtest or malware proof must be rerun; if only a design note changed without affecting the release package, use a documented dependency analysis instead of blind requalification.

## 76.4 Physical target versus proxy observations

Support a transparent taxonomy: pure source; simulated reference; browser JS executed; Godot headless imported; Godot replay parity; visible canvas/frame captured; real interactive controller; compiled ROM bytes; emulator play; physical hardware; independent legal/rights/accessibility/security; authorized release. Some may be independent parallel dimensions rather than a single ladder. For example compiled PSG table parity can be true while audible sound is untested. Do not conflate an SVG raster source with a captured game frame, or a signed reviewer HMAC with actual human play.

For each target and genre, require only relevant independent evidence; never force a retro 2BPP cartridge to prove PC ray tracing. Conversely a 3D Godot target cannot claim physical rendering solely from a pixel-tile source test. The producer of a proof and its reviewer must have distinct roles where policy requires. A report showing an "unblocked" total without enumerating target qualifications is insufficient for release.

## 76.5 Cross-PR integration and conflict safety

Under heavy autonomous throughput, dozens of drafts may change mirrored AI trees, machine contracts, game planners, CI gates and source encoders. Build an exact-head path/owner/dependency comparison before rebases or merges. Resolve canonical AI-tree parity and any mandatory project source index using existing architecture. Do not combine 250-file quota batches blindly. A merge is allowed only after current-head required checks pass and no unresolved security, provenance, native, install or release hold is waived. Source volume is not a maturity metric.
