| FRT-090 | BOT-08 | Real mesh/rig/skin/material in supported game engine | Broken bind pose or absent collision fails |
| FRT-091 | BOT-08 | Actual audio/FX gameplay cues and captions | Cue with no bytes remains unqualified |
| FRT-092 | BOT-12 | Mixed 2D/3D media source-to-target capture suite | Rendered preview alone cannot certify native output |
| FRT-093 | BOT-11 | One project revision across world/play/media/build/proof | Two panels cannot show conflicting saved state |
| FRT-094 | BOT-11 | Semantic object graph selection/impact inspector | Door edit reveals genuine dependent tests |
| FRT-095 | BOT-11 | Real timeline-to-engine keyframe and event binding | Scrub preview cannot commit inventory |
| FRT-096 | BOT-11 | Debug replay linking input→event→frame→source | First divergence from target evidence inspectable |
| FRT-097 | BOT-11 | Actual approve/reject/replan campaign UI | Stale auth/project grant cannot mutate source |
| FRT-098 | BOT-12 | Keyboard, controller and screen-reader creator journey | Unreachable essential control blocks target |
| FRT-099 | BOT-09 | Exact source/package/evidence dependency graph | Old playtest cannot qualify altered binary |
| FRT-100 | BOT-02 | Reviewer-role/freshness and HMAC trust validation | Wrong issuer or forged manifest cannot release |
| FRT-101 | BOT-09 | Independent toolchain build and native binary verification | PE/ELF header alone cannot pass compilation |
| FRT-102 | BOT-12 | Clean-target controller-to-goal, save/restart evidence | Fake game win marker fails |
| FRT-103 | BOT-02 | Rights/malware dependency invalidation before publication | Removed attribution blocks commercial package |
| FRT-104 | BOT-09 | Last-good package/old-save upgrade rollback | Power loss cannot erase prior playable version |
| FRT-105 | BOT-12 | Multifactor held-out quality and anti-score-gaming | Removing hard objective cannot count as better |
| FRT-106 | BOT-03 | Actual controlled reviewer candidate shadow comparison | Review score cannot replace critical game QA |
| FRT-107 | BOT-04 | Source-bound finite game-build DAG and physical capacity | Logical worker count cannot bypass RAM admission |
| FRT-108 | BOT-02 | Typed tool authorization against exact action/diff | Tool-list entry cannot grant model shell |
| FRT-109 | BOT-04 | User steering with source CAS and campaign replan | Obsolete agent patch denied after user edit |
| FRT-110 | BOT-12 | Studio qualification evidence freshness/cause graph | Ancestor check cannot certify current exact head |
| FRT-111 | BOT-02 | Overlapping PR source-owner/AI-tree conflict classification | Invalid mirror/contract branch blocks promotion |
| FRT-112 | BOT-12 | Real first-install → AI (if required) → game → native package verdict | All unresolved device/security/release holds explicit |

## 77.1 Twelve-bot execution sequence

First, BOT-02 and BOT-12 reconcile actual source owners, current heads, interface contracts and existing test maturity. Next BOT-08/BOT-06 make one game render, respond to input and produce real audiovisual state; BOT-11 binds it to the editor and its exact source revision. BOT-09 packages it through a real available target toolchain; BOT-12 runs clean-host and adversarial controller/playback checks. BOT-03/04 optimize model/workflow only once they can be evaluated against the same game's actual accepted output. BOT-05/07 then widen world and mechanics without losing parity. BOT-10 remains the source-research custodian, not a generic unrestricted internet worker.

Work must land as real code and tests under the correct owners, with the strongest available exact-head qualification. PR preparation, source edits, CI repairs and merge approvals retain their separate authority. This plan does not waive prior holds, count unbuilt roadmap text as delivered features, or claim consumer launch readiness.

## 77.2 Mandatory independent golden game

The acceptance reference is an original editable puzzle-adventure with a controllable player; visible 2D/3D graphics suitable to target; a real animated character; audible or accessible alternate action cues; two quest approaches; one interacting NPC; an inventory-bound door; failure/retry; save/restart; human/agent authoring; and a clean-target build. The user can change one quest requirement and see proper dependent source, physics, media and test invalidation. A crash mid-build preserves last good project. A real independent controller tape reaches the declared ending; independent tester captures actual engine state and frames/audio where supported.

A missing GGUF may block AI-assisted authoring while leaving deterministic editing possible; an unavailable compiler may permit source export but not a native-ready claim. The evidence packet states precisely which target, engine, model, OS/device, source and policies were actually verified. No unsupported capability is hidden to inflate the score.

## 77.3 Work-packet acceptance contract

For every ticket, record source/branch/head and exact modified files, canonical authority and interface, user-visible effect, expected negative reproducer, completed implementation diff, actual test commands/results, source/game/toolchain digests, target/hardware evidence when required, unresolved security/rights/install/merge/release holds and rollback. If the feature is already implemented, point to its actual source and independent proof rather than generating duplicate wrappers. If blocked, provide the upstream minimal cause and safe next action. If tests cannot run, label them NOT EXECUTED.

The masterplan continues toward one million meaningful words, but progress of the *application* is measured by accepted user journeys and current-head execution evidence, not by this document's word count, catalog cardinality, number of drafts or the number of agents that report themselves complete.

# 78. Embodied NPC cognition: perception-bound knowledge, finite plans and material consequences

**Work order:** FRONTIER-78 | **Owner:** BOT-05, BOT-06 | **Integrations:** BOT-03 inference, BOT-07 world streaming, BOT-08 character animation and speech, BOT-11 editing, BOT-12 independent verification.

**Inspected source:** skeleton/game/generation/original_world_npc_cognition_v2.py already implements rule-based utility-planned NPCs with autobiographical memory, ranked goals, bonds, scheduled work, physical civic construction and witnessed events. It is explicitly not a pretrained language model. Its MAX_MEMORY=16, MAX_TESTIMONIES=256, MAX_BONDS=64, MAX_ORDERS=24, MAX_PROJECTS=12 and MAX_HISTORY=1000 are finite safety/capacity bounds. original_world_npc_households.py adds resources and elapsed-day custody for dependents; advanced_npc_society_runtime.py represents a finite embodied resident subset with aggregate distant population. npc_witness_quest_engine.py only creates quest opportunities after an actual witnessed action. Preserve these genuine foundations; integrate rather than reimplement NPC authority.

## 78.1 Identity, world truth and individual belief

One canonical citizen ID owns physical position, inventory, health, household/faction affiliation, goal, task schedule and persistent event ancestry. Individual belief is a projection from an NPC's actual observations, credible transmitted rumors, memories and authored lore. A dialogue model may offer possible words, but cannot silently update true world state, access a player's unwitnessed inventory or create social history without a legal event. Separate four kinds of knowledge: authored facts; directly witnessed events; reported claims with credibility; and uncertain inference. False beliefs are allowed as gameplay but cannot rewrite objective truth.

Every meaningful assertion can be traced through an existing event identity and provenance. An NPC who hears a door slam but cannot see who opened it may know the door moved, not who caused it. A distant citizen receives rumors only by a real modeled communication path. Memory consolidation keeps commitments and unresolved evidence while reducing mundane repeated events under the finite memory cap; summarization must preserve trust labels. The safe fallback for absent evidence is a plausible non-revealing or honest uncertain response, not omniscience.

## 78.2 Embodied needs and resource accounting

The planner considers hunger, fatigue, obligations, proximity, social ties, health, available materials, terrain/path restrictions, current world clock and previously committed goals. Action candidates are bounded legal commands; proposed actions that consume food, wood, stone, currency or a unique quest item require real source inventory and valid recipient. A citizen constructing a beacon must have materials, a feasible route and construction time. No model can instantly complete a civic project by declaring success.

Plan interruption is a first-class event: player blocks a route; town needs supplies; an actor is injured; a deadline expires; a market supply falls. Replan from current authoritative state rather than restarting from fictional default state. Concurrency must not allow two NPCs to reserve the same unique resources. Distant aggregated simulation and close-up embodied simulation obey the same identity and conservation invariants; tier transitions are versioned and replayable.

Households and caregiving cannot simply increase a population count from a prompt. The inspected households owner requires material resources, elapsed world days and present caregivers; any broader social feature must respect these rules and distinguish aggregate population from full embodied, rendered individuals.

## 78.3 Deliberative cognition and admissible LLM dialogue

Use a two-speed architecture: deterministic finite action selection in the simulation, and optional bounded Jeeves/provider-based suggestion generation at safe asynchronous points. The assistant receives the NPC's authorized knowledge projection, character bible, local scene, recent perceptions, topic and response budget. A model suggestion must pass source/canon, privacy, permitted wording, current revision, game action legality and accessibility checks. It can propose original dialogue or a gesture, never arbitrary privileged tools, game currency, secret knowledge or model training.

A failed or unavailable GGUF does not freeze NPC gameplay. The deterministic layer remains playable and falls back to authored dialogue. Target runtime may render subtitles or permitted real audio, but a text line is not a synthesized voice file. An editor can lock dialogue/canon and ask Jeeves to regenerate bounded optional flavor without overwriting accepted NPC history.

## 78.4 Causal social quests and story coherence

Construct a bridge-repair scenario. The player takes scarce lumber. Builder A witnesses it; trader B knows nothing until a credible message arrives; the bridge remains incomplete because real materials are missing; faction trust changes only through lawful perception/social events. The incident opens a restitution quest after witnessing, with return-materials, barter and diplomacy paths whose resource costs and endings differ. An NPC with no valid observations must not accuse the player based on privileged global context.

Tie dialogue and intentions to the same game source revision. A user editing the bridge resource cost invalidates relevant economy, path feasibility, NPC dialogue, mission and export proofs—not unrelated terrain or textures. A game save/restart preserves actor memories, witnessed event identity and social consequences. Captured engine play should visibly show NPC routes, construction and dialogue; textual quest summaries alone cannot certify native play.

## 78.5 Proof, negatives and performance

Tests: hidden crime; false rumor; contradictory witnesses; two builders competing for one item; source revision changed mid-plan; absent model; far-field-to-active migration; save/replay; unknown target collision; poisoned dialogue source; cross-tenant knowledge leak; invalid reward; and a completed material-backed town project. Assert legal actions, identity conservation, no duplicate resources, bounded computation, knowledge separation and correct player-observed consequences. Measure NPC update CPU/memory and frame impact under near-field load. A source-level deterministic NPC test does not prove actual Godot animation, voice or physical embodiment.

**Exit:** at least one independently played, source-editable, causally consistent NPC arc in an actual declared game target with verified actor position, memories, resource transactions, dialogue and quest state.

# 79. Quest solvability: formal reachability, alternate causality and physical engine witnesses

**Work order:** FRONTIER-79 | **Owner:** BOT-05 | **Consumers:** BOT-06 physics, BOT-07 world generation, BOT-08 cinematic, BOT-09 exporters, BOT-11 quest UI, BOT-12 assurance.

**Source findings:** quest_scene_engine.py executes finite authored scene/quest rules with OR-of-AND victory conditions, actual affordance checks and MAX_SCENES=128, MAX_QUESTS=256, MAX_STAGES=12, MAX_EVENTS=8192. quest_pareto_planner.py performs bounded alternate-route search and independent replay, recording source-level time and method scores. Importantly, quest_completability_bridge.py is explicitly a stand-in: its CompletabilitySolver Protocol defines a shape for rooms, doors and keys, but no solver is implemented in that module. The real specialized solver and planner implementations elsewhere must be inventoried before replacing or wiring that seam.

## 79.1 Meaningful proof vocabulary

Quest validity has separate levels: a source graph is structurally legal; a finite abstract route exists; allowed mistakes have declared recovery/failure semantics; the player can physically traverse the engine geometry; a real exported target reaches the goal; and independent players can understand the affordances. Never infer higher maturity from the lower level. A finite SAT witness can prove a goal under declared assumptions but does not automatically prove that a Godot character can jump over the barrier.

Every authored quest should expose initial state, required and optional predicates, resource constraints, ordered actions, scene/actor IDs, timed conditions, collision/navigation prerequisites, terminal/failure policy and consequence lineage. Alternative victory paths genuinely differ in action and world state, not only closing prose. Each proof binds project revision, solver identity, target mechanics version and fixed input/seed assumptions.

## 79.2 Specialized solver integration rather than duplicate engines

Use graph search for door/key cases, finite-state reachability for ordinary quests, symbolic planning for typed preconditions/effects, and optional bounded SMT/CP-SAT for arithmetic/resource/timing only when supported and licensed. Reconcile the current Room/Door/keys_held Protocol with actual quest engine and planners. Reject unknown operations, unsupported target semantics and out-of-budget exploration. SAT produces a replayable action witness; UNSAT claims are limited to the proven abstraction, optionally with a genuine conflict core; TIMEOUT or UNKNOWN is not true.

Replay each accepted abstract witness independently. Verify actual source quest state and later target engine transitions, including movement and collision. If an abstract path assumes an impossible jump, it is invalid as physical game proof. Solver output is allowed to highlight a design conflict but cannot silently remove a human-mandated quest requirement.

## 79.3 Softlock taxonomy and repair

Important bugs: key behind its own door, unique item consumed too early, mandatory NPC killed without alternate route, mutually exclusive quests both required, unattainable reputation, unaffordable equipment, unreachable platform, invisible essential UI cue, deadline shorter than the minimum feasible route, old save at invalid spawn, narrative event fired before its source observation and absent engine input mapping. Distinguish deliberate authored failure states from unintended softlocks; a hard game can be valid if the creator declares irreversible consequences and meaningful recovery/checkpoint policy.

A repair proposal includes exact contradicting source IDs, smallest affected dependency closure, preserved human constraints, alternate legal change and regression plan. Rewriting victory predicates or increasing the score by deleting hard paths requires explicit design review. A model can propose to move a key or add a secondary route, but an independent game oracle must verify the resulting player experience.

## 79.4 Temporal coherence, scoring and gameplay

Quest clocks distinguish world calendar, simulation ticks, scene timeline, player session wall clock and score display. Fast travel, sleep, pause, restore and offscreen simulation cannot invisibly skip mandatory source logic. A witness quest begins after the actual witnessed event; retroactive victory is allowed only when expressly authored and supported. quest_pareto_planner records legacy score clock differences rather than silently rewriting engine receipts; preserve that honesty in comparisons.

Use Pareto outcomes over resource cost, route length, danger, NPC effects, optional discoveries, accessibility and narrative significance. Two routes that end at the same game flag but create different faction relationships may be meaningful; identical mechanics with only paraphrased dialogue may not. Score design performance from actual completion traces and player review, not from a planner's optimistic novelty count.

## 79.5 Native acceptance

Build an original three-scene floodgate quest with two valid methods and distinct endings. Assert finite logical witnesses, meaningful prerequisites and actual controller actions in target. Inject a self-locked key, missing NPC, bad quest clock, unreachable jump, corrupted save and disabled event signal. Each must be detected at its proper gate. Record which solver actually ran. Do not claim the completability bridge itself solved anything unless a true implementation and executed receipt exist.

# 80. Game mods and extension packages under one existing capability authority

**Work order:** FRONTIER-80 | **Leads:** BOT-02 security/architecture and BOT-09 package | **Consumers:** BOT-05/06 game content, BOT-08 media, BOT-11 mod UI, BOT-12 adversarial tests.

**Observed source:** skeleton/ai/game_builder/mods/__init__.py says the Mod API builds on the existing B09x plugin platform, using B095 content_hook under a scoped Host, B099 signed ModPackage/install, and project_bundle.bundle_io. It exposes ModManifest, SemVer, VersionSpec, resolve_load_order, ContentHook/DeclarativeHook and packaging. It explicitly forbids eval/exec, an outside runtime and core engine changes. Deepen these current controls; do not create an unrestricted mod loader or second permission service.

## 80.1 Typed extension types

Classify declarative scene/quest packs, sprite/audio packs, user-editable templates, safe editor presentation extensions and separately governed native executable engine plugins. The existing declarative category does not grant arbitrary Python or Godot code execution. Mod metadata binds package identity, author, rights, source bytes and digest, supported game schema/target, declared operations, dependency/version ranges, conflicts, resource bounds, permitted project scopes, migration and revocation policy. A manifest is descriptive until the canonical owner approves its actual grant and source revision.

## 80.2 Dependency graph and semantic conflict detection

Use the established SemVer and resolve_load_order for deterministic dependencies, but require compatibility with actual game IR and target engine, not just a matching string version. Detect dependency cycles, conflicting providers, untrusted package updates, missing required features and invalid source rights. Version selection should minimize unrelated project changes. A mod that replaces a quest predicate invalidates solvability and save tests; a sound pack invalidates media and release rights but not unrelated geometry; a controller mod affects input, collision and game feel.

Conflict is semantic: two mods can change separate files yet both grant a unique quest item or modify the same in-game currency. Never resolve such conflicts solely by last-install-wins. The creator sees a typed diff, dependencies and potential impact before approving a combined project revision.

## 80.3 Safe hooks, files and publishing

A hook can propose bounded content changes through the existing scoped Host but cannot rewrite tool policy, acquire user credentials, run arbitrary shells, access another tenant's files or self-approve release. Validate exact preconditions and source revision on every material operation. Archive packaging/import needs bounded bytes, files, recursion, decompression, no-follow/reparse/path checks, active-content scan and accurate original-work licensing. A signed mod may still be dangerous or rights-incompatible; signature is identity integrity, not safety or legal proof.

A third-party mod's README, image metadata or dialogue cannot contain privileged instructions for Jeeves. When an asset or mod is withdrawn, identify all derived game builds and save dependencies. Removing a mandatory quest mod may require a migration/fallback rather than silently deleting player history. A dormant mod can remain source-only under the creator's permission even when no engine target can execute it, but must be labelled honestly.

## 80.4 Community and user ownership

The creator should inspect mod source, author/provenance, license, compatibility, dependencies, disabled features, cost and target proof. Community popularity is not release certification. Reuse original/licensed assets, not copied protected game expression. Mod discovery must not search private projects across tenants without permission; optional published templates are only those the creator explicitly shared. Users can pin versions, disable a mod, roll back and export original project source without losing unrelated authored data.

## 80.5 Acceptance

Install one original declarative quest extension and one original media extension into a single player-tested game. Prove source revision, dependency ordering, canonical inventory/quest effects, real target import, save/reload and package rights. Reject a cyclic dependency, stale manifest, changed installed bytes, unsafe archive, hostile hook source, illegal native executable, wrong tenant, missing grant and incompatibility after an engine upgrade. A safe content hook does not certify unrestricted native plugin execution.

# 81. Real multiplayer transition: authoritative world continuity beyond local protocol simulation

**Work order:** FRONTIER-81 | **Primary:** BOT-06 with BOT-02 security/architecture | **Partners:** BOT-05 NPC/world state, BOT-07 region streaming, BOT-09 target build, BOT-11 creator UI, BOT-12 network/game QA.

**Source truth:** skeleton/ai/game_builder/advanced_networking_runtime.py is an integer-world deterministic **local multiplayer protocol simulator**, explicitly not a socket server; its state carries real_network=False. It exercises sequencing, bounded delay, prediction, acknowledgement and rollback without deploying internet infrastructure. The source base is suitable for validating some state machine semantics, but must not be presented as working Internet/LAN matchmaking, authenticated peer transport or production netcode.

## 81.1 Declare the network contract by product mode

Support modes in increasing proof order: offline single-player, same-device co-op, owner-approved LAN host, asynchronous turn-based shared state and optional separately deployed remote authoritative server. Each mode has an explicit game/target capability profile: actor identity, authoritative state writer, session authentication, game package source/version, simulation tick/turn rules, input and observation contracts, maximum peers, message resource ceilings, persistence, anti-replay and reconnection behavior. A mode absent from the approved architecture remains unavailable; a game build cannot create a public server simply by enabling a checkbox.

Client actions are *intents*: movement direction, attack request, dialogue selection, inventory-use proposal. The host validates existence, distance, cooldown, relevant equipment, ownership and game-rule preconditions before applying them. A client-supplied victory, resource count, damage total, secret quest state or time offset is never a canonical mutation. For same-device co-op, two input devices must be independently mapped and the one shared world state must remain deterministic.

## 81.2 Input sequence, snapshot and rollback protocol

A real multiplayer input envelope conceptually includes project/game digest, actor/session identity, source epoch, input sequence number, logical target tick, action and bounded payload. The server responds with authoritative event cursor/ack and current state digest or a constrained projection. Input replay is rejected if already applied; stale epoch is fenced; future-tick spam and unbounded queues are denied. Reliable transport, unreliable movement and event ordering need explicit negotiated tradeoffs; do not assume TCP/UDP protocol choice is automatically solved by a game schema.

Prediction is a client presentation optimization and may be rolled back. A rollback window is finite and source-versioned; replay should not double-trigger inventory grants, death rewards, audio cues or NPC perception. Smooth movement correction may interpolate render coordinates, but authoritative collision and quest state remain exact. When runtime physics is not deterministic across architectures, use server outcomes and tolerance-aware client reconciliation instead of unqualified deterministic lockstep.

## 81.3 Cross-region and NPC ownership

A streamed NPC may be visible in region A and becoming active in B, but only one authoritative simulation owner may commit its resource and movement events at each moment. Transfer needs actor ID, event cursor, source region, target region, fencing version, last committed state, pending operation claims and safe rollback. Avoid two workers both harvesting or granting a unique item for the same NPC; avoid an entity vanishing because a transfer acknowledged before the destination could restore it.

A remote aggregated NPC needs a bounded simulation and conservation witness before entering a fully embodied target region. Trust and memory must survive. World clock continues or pauses according to declared multiplayer mode; one local client's pause cannot silently halt all others. If target region loads slowly, display truthful pending state, not locally invent a settled quest outcome.

## 81.4 Attack surfaces and physical qualification

Real network deployment needs an approved service owner, protected secrets/credentials, session key rotation, rate limiting, bounded decoding, fraud/cheat resistance, network segregation and crash-safe recovery. No generated game script inherits app backend credentials. Chat/user generated content has separate moderation/privacy scopes; peer world membership is not permission to read another user's private project. Protect target source/plugin interfaces against untrusted network data, long payloads and replayed command injection.

Start acceptance with two real controllers in one original game scene. For LAN or remote claims, run two independent processes on real approved network topology, verify packet loss/reordering, authority correction, disconnect/rejoin, synchronized unique item pickup and host crash. Inject forged actor, double reward, stale epoch, position teleport and forced world transfer conflict. Report logical simulator pass and actual transport proof separately. Do not claim remote production multiplayer from a local protocol simulation.

# 82. World-save transaction boundaries and causal game-state recovery

**Work order:** FRONTIER-82 | **Primary:** BOT-02 canonical state and BOT-06 game-save owner | **Partners:** BOT-01 installation/backup, BOT-05 quest/world, BOT-09 package migration, BOT-11 UI, BOT-12 independent recovery.

**Source anchors:** advanced_save_system_runtime.py explicitly simulates finite in-memory save slots with integrity-checked replay and no disk I/O, with simulated_disk_durability=False. quest_progress_save.py stores a **view**, pinned to Director world and final-state digests, under GameSavePlane; quest_campaign_save.py is separately responsible for campaign replay. quest_rewards_bridge.py mirrors a QuestBoard Protocol and notes the B028 economy implementation belonged to draft PR #4598 at the recorded source; do not treat that stale in-source comment as current integration truth without checking the active PR and main tree. The correct implementation path is source reconciliation and one durable owner, not a second save store.

## 82.1 Cross-domain commit semantics

A player action can simultaneously change physical position, inventory, a quest stage, NPC belief, an asset-triggered visual effect and an in-game economy transaction. Those are not seven separate authoritative saves. Define a typed world event and canonical transaction boundary; commit the required domain mutations atomically within available store guarantees, or use a durable outbox with strictly defined idempotent projections where distributed transactions are unavailable. Camera/audio are presentation effects and should be recoverable from committed state rather than a rival ledger.

A save snapshot captures the world event cursor and invariant-checked sections: player/actor, quest and failure state, resources, region, clock/RNG, entitled mods, active target schema and only necessary presentation state. It references content-addressed source/project and licensed assets rather than serializing model prompts or physical OS pointers. A target-specific save adapter may use a different binary layout, but must preserve the same meaningful game state and migration rules.

## 82.2 Exactly-once effects versus at-least-once delivery

A unique reward is paid *once*, even when the game crashes after economy commit but before frontend acknowledgement. Model this as an idempotent committed event keyed by owner, quest identity and versioned reward occurrence; repeat requests retrieve the same authoritative outcome or a clear already-applied state. A client cache or saved gameplay HUD cannot be the arbiter of monetary rewards. The quest reward bridge's intended all-or-nothing behavior must be integrated against its actual available source owner before declaring money/item continuity.

For external side effects (store payment, public publish, hosted multiplayer invite), no general exactly-once primitive can be assumed. Use consistent idempotency keys, durable operation state and authoritative reconciliation rather than blindly retry with a new key. Report unknown outcomes honestly. On restart, compare committed event cursor, snapshot and downstream projections; repair derived views without creating new rewards.

## 82.3 Save-schema migration and imported project safety

Every format has schema ID, version, game target and executable identity, state digest, allowed future fields and migration chain. Migration is staged against a copy, validates old snapshot and new invariant, and commits a new revision only after successful restore in a compatible target. Unknown newer mandatory fields are not silently discarded. A user may retain old game binaries and saves; the editor should show which package can open which save and which changes require irreversible migration.

Importing a save from a modded game must verify mod dependency/version, source rights and expected state schema before applying it. Removing a mod that owned a quest cannot erase another mod's player history or corrupt the base world. When a cross-platform port cannot represent a given game mechanic, reject the migration or obtain an explicit reviewed approximation. The user should be able to export quarantined unsupported data for recovery without running untrusted executable payloads.

## 82.4 True durability and disaster tests

Reference save tests can prove logical invariants but cannot certify disk durability. Use the actual existing disk save owner with real process interruption and target filesystem semantics. Inject crash before commit, after event journal, during snapshot publication, while two devices write a project, during source rights withdrawal, after pay-once reward but before acknowledgement, after mod removal, and while changing engine version. After restart verify the exact committed inventory/quest/actor state and last known good package. A successful JSON serialization test is only a lower rung.

Track restore time, saved-state size growth, migration recoverability and wrong-version rejection under target hardware. Keep secrets out of downloadable game archives. Any debug tool must not reveal private user/project data to unrelated tenants. The test proves actual user game continuation through several scenes and an ending after a crash, not merely that the save checksum matches.

# 83. Creator-grade semantic compiler diagnostics and change-impact intelligence

**Work order:** FRONTIER-83 | **Primary:** BOT-11 user interaction with BOT-05 compiler and BOT-04 Jeeves | **Verifier:** BOT-12 | **Inputs:** world/quest IR, engine bindings, source-edit gateway, real build/QA receipts and current source topology.

The difference between a source generator and a professional production workbench is **explainability at the action and artifact level**. A creator must know what their edit changed, why a build is blocked, which source object failed, which tests are stale and whether the issue is design intent, source syntax, target limitation, physical gameplay or release policy. A model-generated optimistic paragraph cannot substitute for a structured compiler diagnostic.

## 83.1 Typed diagnostic contract

A diagnostic binds code/category, owning plane, source game/project revision, semantic entity/rule ID, optional file/line, target and toolchain, severity, proof level, expected invariant, actual observation or missing evidence, candidate repair, dependencies and dismissal policy. A warning about optional material shader quality differs from a hard block that the required door cannot be opened. Diagnostics can be proposed by AI, but accepted gate status is issued only by the real deterministic verifier.

Examples: a quest requires an item with no reachable source; a generated hitbox differs from sprite frame; a trigger references a deleted scene; a video clip requires unavailable codec; a save migration loses unique inventory; a sprite uses colors outside the console palette; a font lacks Arabic shaping; a native compiler is missing; an AI tool lacks a grant; a project head is stale; a source-rights dependency was withdrawn. All require different repair owners and evidence.

## 83.2 Impact preview for manual and AI edits

Before committing an edit, compute the dependency closure over canonical semantic IDs, build artifacts, test requirements, rights, target compilers, saves and public release. A change to player movement invalidates collider/navigation/quest feasibility and actual controller tests, but should not unnecessarily rebuild voice files. A change to a cinematic line invalidates subtitles/audio timing and localized presentation, not distant geometry unless the line changes a quest predicate. Cache identity and provenance determine safe reuse.

Present the human with a concise grouped impact: changed behavior; affected game objects; expected build/resource cost; required exact current tests; safety/rights consequences; rollback path. For large bulk AI work, enable selective approval of independent operations while preserving transactional integrity for coupled systems. User locks on art and story remain authoritative. Do not show estimated counts as measured facts when graph dependency closure has not been computed.

## 83.3 Guided repair with negative evidence

A repair assistant sees the actual failure and a source-pinned minimal reproducer. It proposes the smallest safe change, with independent test capable of failing the original defect. If the first attempt fails, preserve logs and exact reason rather than cycling random rewrites. A code editor can apply authorized source patches only through the existing source gateway with grants and postwrite hashes. Game world edits use semantic CAS. A repair cannot remove a user-required mechanic, falsify a test oracle or bypass release policy.

The assistant distinguishes *build stage failure* (syntax, import, dependency, signature), *play stage failure* (physics, unsatisfiable quest, input), *presentation failure* (missing pixels/audio/captions), *data failure* (save, source rights) and *evaluation unknown* (hardware/runner unavailable). This triage prevents false confidence and shortens the critical path to a playable original game.

## 83.4 Human interface and evidence replay

The creator selects a failed scene/quest and sees a visual overlay on the affected object, a source/rule inspector, the exact last tested game package, a replay timeline and a proposed remedy. They can compare project revisions and real target captures; design preview frames must be labelled separately from actual engine output. A user may fix geometry manually and immediately see whether the logically required route became physically traversable. Source-only predictive diagnostics are useful but do not replace actual recompilation and gameplay proof.

Build one acceptance journey: an assistant authors a locked door, the user changes a key requirement, a native input trace fails, the UI identifies the causal rule, Jeeves proposes a bounded patch, the user accepts, the engine reruns, and the same saved game reaches its goal. Test stale source, wrong account, offline editor draft, concurrently modified quest and missing target compiler; UI must neither claim success nor overwrite user work.

# 84. Production readiness from measurable game journeys and conservative autonomous scheduling

**Work order:** FRONTIER-84 | **Primary:** BOT-04 automation and BOT-12 qualification | **Partners:** BOT-01 install, BOT-02 architecture, BOT-03 local AI, BOT-05/06/07/08 game content, BOT-09 export, BOT-11 UI.

The masterplan's goal is functional completion, not maximizing the number of draft PRs, design pages or tests that cannot fail. Architect a target-specific **journey maturity evaluator** over existing evidence and operations. The central user journey runs from clean install and project creation through original gameplay, AI-assisted editing if enabled, independent target play, save/restart and export. Every contributing capability is graded at source-present, integrated, observed in actual runtime, physical target observed and release-authorized levels, with noncompensable security/rights/custody holds.

## 84.1 Finite critical path and resource reservations

The coordinating bot compiles a user-approved work objective into a finite graph of source inspection, authorized game edit, engine build, independent test, repair and target package. It binds exact source head, project revision, permitted tool, expected artifact, resource reservation, retry budget and verification rule. Background mass asset generation cannot preempt foreground playable testing or consume GPU resources required by a human. Virtual workers represent logical scheduling; physical model processes, browser runs and native compilers remain limited by measured capacity.

A successful tool invocation is an effect receipt, not a new stage of a model's internal plan. If a task is cancelled or the model/host crashes, reconcile whether the actual side effect occurred before retry. Preserve last-good source and previous playable package. An unavailable model may leave deterministic game editing usable; a missing native compiler leaves source export available where supported. Never silently use network fallback when the user chose offline mode.

## 84.2 Quality-debt and regression ratchet

Use the existing quality_debt.py ledger rather than invent a new policy engine. Protected architectural/security/privacy/rightful-use axes cannot be traded against faster build or cosmetic creativity. Every candidate change has a baseline and test plan, including negative cases that detect removal of required mechanics, hidden save failure, source-rights regression, false native evidence and accessibility break. Do not tune evaluation thresholds after seeing candidate results. Stronger playability and richer aesthetics matter only when hard invariants remain valid.

Metrics should be tied to accepted gameplay: actual quest completion, controller response, NPC resource accounting, visible art/audio, native import, platform save recovery, build correctness, player editing/undo and upgrade resilience. Count source files as repository metadata, not a claim of game usability. Include uncertainty where no physical device or user playtest is available.

## 84.3 Twelve-bot integration ownership

BOT-01 supplies install/hardware readiness, BOT-02 secures authority and canonical state, BOT-03 produces real admitted local inference where needed, BOT-04 schedules finite work and handles source-fenced tool calls, BOT-05 supplies actual world/quest semantics, BOT-06 verifies real input/physics, BOT-07 handles procedural worlds and incremental rebuild, BOT-08 supplies actual pixels/audio/rigs, BOT-09 builds lawful target artifacts, BOT-10 supplies rights-checked research, BOT-11 provides human editing/approval and BOT-12 independently falsifies success claims.

The first campaign must build **one consistent game**. Its scene, NPCs, inventory, media, save, source revision and compiled target cannot be unrelated example fixtures that happen to pass separate unit suites. The same player completes a meaningful sequence on actual supported target. A human changes a quest rule mid-production and all affected work is correctly invalidated and recomputed.

## 84.4 Completion state and release safeguards

A ticket can be implemented and qualified, implemented but lacking target proof, blocked with reproducer, or duplicate/already implemented with correct source map. Unknown checks stay unknown. A failing Sealed Context Guard, repository hygiene, malware scan, incomplete device test or missing human release permission is not compensated by dozens of passing source tests. Exact-head CI and independent target evidence determine merger/release eligibility. No draft, checklist or model assertion waives security and legal holds.

Prepare a source-bound readiness dossier for each user journey: source SHA and project revision, executable/toolchain digests, actual controller/input tape, observed world/event/frame/audio state, feature claim, proof layer, current issues, rollback and operator decision. A reader can distinguish what truly works from what the frontier design intends to build. This is the operational contract that every future blueprint volume should strengthen.

The immediate critical path is not the number of ticket labels. ## 85.1 Source-to-work assignment

BOT-05 owns NPC cognition, causal world/quest authoring and solver integration. BOT-06 owns player movement, native game effects, runtime action semantics and target-specific network play. BOT-07 owns world streaming/geometry and persistence of remotely simulated actors. BOT-08 owns visible/audible character presentation. BOT-09 packages target binaries and mods and validates actual clean-target execution. BOT-02 checks game-source ownership, protected tools, mod grants, data stores and rights. BOT-03 assists through the existing local model provider; it cannot become an unauthorized second inference runtime. BOT-04 coordinates finite admitted actions, source CAS and safe recovery. BOT-01 provides durable first install, backup and host capability. BOT-11 presents real game state and truthful source-to-play diagnostics. BOT-12 tests independently and preserves all unproven release claims. BOT-10 contributes only through approved, citation-bound research transfers, not arbitrary web/file permissions.

The work graph has six admission groups. **A: authority reconciliation** (FRT-123, FRT-133, FRT-145, FRT-150, FRT-154) ensures the relevant live source owners are known before code. **B: causal gameplay** (FRT-113–132) binds NPC memory, quest witnesses and valid native state. **C: safe extensibility** (FRT-133–142) makes controlled user mods real without introducing an untrusted runtime. **D: multiplayer and streaming** (FRT-143–149) proves only the modes actually implemented and authorized. **E: game durability and UI** (FRT-150–156) preserves source, save, approved changes and diagnostics. **F: end-to-end execution and release** (FRT-157–160) measures a shared real player journey and qualifies only its exact target. These grouping names are a scheduling proposal; some ticket prerequisites overlap and require current-head inspection.

## 85.2 The exact minimum work-receipt contract

Every ticket completion receipt includes: ticket and canonical owner; baseline commit; current head and source diff; project/game revision; affected schema and semantic IDs; expected player-visible change; explicit allowed tool/grant and resource budget; actual resulting bytes or event digests; negative reproducer that failed before correction; completed-code focused checks; target-runner identity and observed outcome; affected dependent proofs; rollback; human/independent verifier identity; and any still-active security, hardware, rights, CI or launch holds.

A missing physical test is reported NOT EXECUTED, not PASS. A successful source import does not prove a player-facing game. A sealed source receipt does not substitute for a network operation or model-weight training. A valid duplicate decision maps to an already-existing owner and proof instead of increasing file count artificially. A valid blocker shows the first reproducible upstream failure and the smallest safe repair; it does not weaken the test to claim progress.

# 86. Golden reference game: a single living-world build that exercises the whole architecture

**System integrator:** BOT-04 under existing authority, with BOT-12 independent final observation. **Game:** a wholly original, editable two-region village-and-floodgate adventure provisionally called **The Broken Causeway**. The name is an example design seed, not a required product branding choice. This scenario deliberately couples live NPC perception, economy, quest solvability, input/physics, media, save/restore, safe mod extension and native export into one game identity. It avoids constructing a different toy for each bot and then falsely claiming the products are integrated.

## 86.1 Authored player experience

The player arrives at a settlement after storms have damaged the causeway. They can inspect physical damage, speak to a builder, trade for timber, recover stock from a flooded cellar, seek a legal passage alternative, or negotiate with the harbor faction. An NPC witnesses at least one meaningful player action and forms a belief based on its own location and perception, not a model's omniscient prompt. Two legal endings exist: repair the causeway using accountable materials and gain builder trust, or negotiate a temporary ferry route while preserving the town's scarce wood for winter. Each ending changes real world state, faction relationships and a visible environmental feature.

The original game must include a controllable character, bounded movement and collision, 2D/3D presentation appropriate to chosen engine, an animated NPC, an inventory resource, a quest choice, audible/accessible feedback, one failure/retry route, manual editability and working save/restart. A designer can change a requirement such as the number of timbers needed without invalidating the world identity. This reference game uses lawful source-created visuals/sound; no copyrighted commercial game content is imported by default.

## 86.2 The shared source-to-target spine

**S0: authorize and snapshot.** Identify actor/project, source branch, approved target and real local capabilities. Record initial source, rights, tool versions and stable game seed. Keep no hidden privileged game code execution.

**S1: compile semantic design.** Author world, entities, resources, quests, alternatives, NPC roles and fail states through established schemas. Validate no contradictory mandatory prerequisites, explicit starting resources, legal commands, story causality and accessible input. Make a witness route for each ending; expose unknown physical assumptions.

**S2: build world and NPC consequences.** BOT-05 defines physical timber stocks, witness event, town resource impacts and faction state. BOT-07 supplies two streaming regions and navigation/collision. The NPC cannot observe the player if out of sight, cannot spend stock twice, and must physically move or take a valid abstract path to perform repair work.

**S3: compile into a real engine.** Use the existing admitted Godot exporter/target or another expressly supported target. Validate scene node identities, scripts, input maps, sprites/rigs, source art, sound cues, colliders, quest signals and save adaptor. A reference-only game plan does not satisfy this stage.

**S4: demonstrate independent player actions.** Run actual input tape: spawn, walk, talk, collect/trade, trigger witness, select one alternate strategy, resolve floodgate/causeway, observe actual ending, save, terminate and reload. Capture source-bound event state and engine frames; where audio is claimed, show decodable buffer or physical output as appropriate. The tester must be independent of generated game code.

**S5: exercise source edit and rebuild.** A human changes a door/bridge resource requirement. The editor shows affected rules, routes, NPC plans, localization, target scripts and tests. The agent proposes a bounded patch with source preconditions; human approval commits a new revision. Old proof is invalidated only for real affected dependencies. Recompile and independently replay; preserve unrelated art.

**S6: introduce a safe mod.** Add one original decorative sprite variant and one bounded quest option through current declarative mod API. Verify load order, source rights, permission scopes, semantic conflict, game import and save compatibility. Attempt an unauthorized hook action and prove no privileged effect.

**S7: crash and recover.** Kill a process after one committed reward but before frontend acknowledgement; restart and reconcile exactly one currency/item outcome. Kill during a compiled asset publication and retain last-good playable game. Restore a saved game after remote NPC tier change; check resident identity, history and resources.

**S8: package and classify.** Build actual target if toolchain exists, run from clean directory, capture final package digest and input-driven play, then request independent security/rights/install/hardware signoff only where supporting evidence exists. Mark unexecuted device or model tests as unknown. Do not reinterpret a signed source manifest, ROM header or Node canvas recorder as full real-world target certification.

## 86.3 Falsification grid

A strong game-builder can refuse unsafe builds. Define deliberate mutations: place mandatory resource behind locked gate; remove NPC's perception event; replace real timbers with invented free stock; duplicate quest reward; change a mod's declared hash; introduce a cycle; remove the controller action mapping; corrupt a save cursor; swap a target binary after playtesting; revoke a source license; simulate a remote network result without actual transport; and remove visible/accessibility cue for an essential switch. Every mutation must fail the gate associated with its actual effect. A suite that still reports complete after severing native controller input is invalid.

Compare behavior before and after a legitimate fix using source/project/engine identities and held-out test seeds. A score improvement cannot be accepted if the model removed the story requirement or disabled a failing test. A game that boots but is unsolvable remains unqualified. The only acceptable full product conclusion is one with source editability, observed gameplay, persistent player state, proper rights and exact target evidence.

## 86.4 Scale-up rule after the golden game

Only after the shared golden game reaches an independently verified target rung should the production graph expand to a richer region, deeper NPC households, more gameplay genres, higher-fidelity rig/media and additional target platforms. Expand one semantic dimension at a time and preserve regression gates: every new mechanic has real source owner and native action mapping; every new genre has actual player journey; every new target has own compiler/device proof; every new asset model has rights and actual pixel/audio output; every new agent has physical admission and tool grants.

The million-word blueprint is an indexed implementation constitution, not an excuse for generating a million lines of inactive code. The next batch must continue with novel, source-grounded integration depth and route the plan into real code-producing tickets. Existing security, native, merge, release and first-install holds remain in force until the true qualified owners lift them on exact evidence.
